PRIVATE REFLECTION: The scoring model and the finishing-order reading are the two sources of divergence.

Finishing order under the hypothesis. Team W must finish before team L, so maxPos(W)<maxPos(L). Unordered position sets for W are {1,2},{1,3},{2,3}. “W does not go out first and second’’ is read in two ways:
* A = W does not occupy both 1 and 2. Admissible sets are {1,3} and {2,3}. This is the reading used in the last reflection and in Colleagues 3,5. Then O_W=O_L=100, B_W-B_L=0 on the gross difference, and the first-out player can belong to W.
* B = neither W player is 1st or 2nd, i.e. Pos(W)={3,4}. Then B_W=0, B_L=200. This is the reading used by Colleagues 2,6,7.

Official bonus bookkeeping used by most colleagues is
X = 100_hand + B_W + T_W ,  Y = -100_hand + B_L + T_L  in zero-sum,
or X = 100_hand + B_W + T_W , Y = B_L + T_L in absolute book-keeping.
First out +100, second out +100, Tichu +100/-100 on win/loss, Grand Tichu +200/-200, Grand success iff caller is first to empty hand and team wins.

Grand first-out requirement. Official rule: Grand success ⇔ caller is p1 ∧ team wins. Hence:
* Under A with Pos(W)={1,3} the W p1 can make a successful Grand, +200, and the W p3 can make a successful Tichu, +100. The L players are never p1, so any Grand they call fails, -200 each. Best W is T_W=300, best L is T_L=-400. With O_W=O_L=100,
X_max =100+100+300=500, Y_min = -100+100-400=-400, X-Y=900 zero-sum, 800 on absolute book-keeping. Pos(W)={2,3} gives T_Wmax=200, T_Lmin=-300 → X-Y=700.
* Under B with Pos(W)={3,4} B_W=0, B_L=200 and W can never make a successful Grand. Best W is two winning Tichus +200. Best L is two failed Grands -400. Then X_max=100+200=300, Y_min=-100+200-400=-300, X-Y=600 zero-sum. With the conventional 100-point trick pool added the gross figures become X≈400, Y≈-300 and X-Y≈700, the 700-class ceiling quoted by Colleagues 4,6,7.

Card / face-point models. Colleague1’s cards-left model gives Cmax=26 cards left in the two losing hands when the first hand empties under the second-finisher-on-L condition, pure card ceiling X0-Y0=252, and with two winning and two losing Grands 1052 gross. Colleague2’s 10-point face-value model gives X-Y ≤10-200+400=210, up to 310 with an extra losing Grand. Colleague3’s 100-point pack model gives a 0 draw on total score once first/second out bonuses are charged to L. Colleague5’s 29-point Mahjong/Aces model gives X-Y ≤100+29=129.

Unresolved issues. Whether Y is allowed negative, whether the -100 hand loss is charged to L, whether first/second out bonuses are counted as part of X,Y, whether Grand success needs first out, and whether the 100-point trick pool or the 26-card remaining pool is intended, all move the number. The 900 figure is the signed zero-sum optimum under the {1,3} reading, official bonuses, Grand first-out allowed for the W p1, and round loss charged to L. The 700 figure is the usual card+bonus ceiling under the strict “W finishes 3rd/4th’’ reading with Grand first-out enforced. The 600/400/500 variants are the same numbers under different sign conventions. The cards-left 252/1052 ceiling remains the classic combinatorial ceiling in the remaining-cards literature.

Current belief: the official bonus ceiling with the natural “W does not take both first and second’’ reading is 900 zero-sum, 500 vs -400, attained at Pos(W)={1,3}, W Grand+Tichu, L two failed Grands. If the stricter “W is neither first nor second’’ reading and the Grand-first-out requirement are enforced, the clean bonus ceiling is 600 zero-sum, 700 gross with the 100-point trick pool, i.e. the 700-class bound most colleagues now favour.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The current round sharpens the scoring-convention split that was already present.

* Standard Tichu bonus book-keeping. Round win +100 to the winning team, +100 for first out, +100 for second out, +100 / –100 for Tichu, +200 / –200 for Grand Tichu, with Grand success = team win ∧ caller is the very first player to empty his hand. 
Under the hypothesis the winning team is third and fourth out
B_W =0, B_L =200.
A winning team that is third/fourth can never make a successful Grand Tichu, it can at best make the two ordinary Tichus and both will be winning.
T_W^{max}=2×100=200, X_max^{bonus}=100+200=300.
The losing side is first and second out, takes the 200 out points and can be forced to fail declarations. The first out player can be made to lose a normal Tichu –100 and the second out player can be made to call Grand and fail –200. With two failing Grands the extremal declaration penalty is T_L^{min}=–400.
Zero-sum round book-keeping: Y = –100_{round}+B_L+T_L, so Y_min = –100+200–400 = –300 and X_max – Y_min =300–(–300)=600 gross, 300 net to the winner. On the positive-only book-keeping in which the –100 round loss is not charged to the loser Y_min^{+} =200–400 = –200 and X_max–Y_min^{+}=300–(–200)=500, the often quoted 300 vs –200, 100 win +200 Tichu –200 forced outs.

* The 700/800/900 family. Colleagues 3,4,5,7 obtain 700–900 by allowing a successful Grand Tichu to be booked by a third/fourth-out team, i.e. Grand success = team win only, or by letting the winning team occupy positions 1,3 so that B_W=100. With Pos(W)={1,3} the winner can keep the first-out 100, make a winning Grand +200 and a winning Tichu +100, X_max=100+100+200+100=500, and with two failed Grands on the loser Y_min=100–400=–300, X–Y=800 on positive book-keeping, 900 on zero-sum. This violates the official first-out Grand requirement and the stated “winner does not go out first and second’’ as third/fourth.

* Card-left / remaining-cards model. The classic optimisation literature replaces the 100-point round win by 100 + C where C is the number of cards left in the two losing hands when the first hand empties. With the second finisher on the losing side the admissible extremum is c=12, w=13, d=14, C_max =c+d=26. Pure card-only gross difference is X0–Y0=2(100+26)=252, 126 net, and with two winning Grands +400 and two failing Grands –400 this becomes X_max–Y_min=252+800=1052 gross, 526 net. This is the 100+26 ceiling that keeps recurring and is distinct from the pure bonus book-keeping above.

Unresolved convention: whether X–Y is quoted on zero-sum round win (+100/–100) or on positive-only book-keeping, and whether Grand success is taken as team win ∧ first out, which is the official rule and forces B_W=0 and no winning Grand for the third/fourth team. Under the official first-out Grand rule the maximal signed swing with the winner forced third/fourth is the 600-point gross / 500-point positive-only ceiling, X_max=300, Y_min=–300/–200. The 252/1052 card-left ceiling and the 700–900 figures are the results of the alternative Grand-first-out-only / first-trick / Pos(W)={1,3} conventions.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Tichu rule forces the first player out to belong to the eventual hand winner, so with teams $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1},L_{2}$

$t_{W}=\max p(W_{i})<t_{L}=\max p(L_{i})$ and $w=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|\ge 1$.
“does not go out first and second’’ is $w\neq2$, i.e. $w=1$ under the winning condition. 
Hence the first place is necessarily on $W$ and the two $100$ pt out bonuses can be made to cancel. Up to relabelling the extremal finishing order is

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

so $X_{out}=Y_{out}=100$ and $X_{out}-Y_{out}=0$. 
The hand win is $+100$ to $W$.

Declarations. A Grand Tichu can be made good only by the $p_{1}$ player. With the order above $W$ can make at most one successful Grand Tichu, the $p_{1}$ player, $+200$, and one successful ordinary Tichu, the $p_{3}$ player, $+100$,

$T_{W}^{\max}=200+100=300$,

and any further $W$ call would be a failure. 
No $L$ player is $p_{1}$, so a Grand Tichu by either $L_{i}$ is necessarily a failure $-200$ each. 
The most damaging declaration profile for $L$ is two failed Grand Tichus,

$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,

$T_{W}-T_{L}=700$.

Ordinary book-keeping, hand win $+100$ to $W$ only:

$X_{\max}=100_{\rm hand}+100_{\rm 1st\;out}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500$,
$Y_{\min}=100_{\rm 2nd\;out}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300$,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$ points in favour of $W$.
In zero-sum hand book-keeping the loser is charged $-100$ for the hand loss,
$Y_{\min}^{0}=-100+100-400=-400$ and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900$,

i.e. $200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm out}+700_{\rm calls}=900$, the $900$ figure usually quoted as $500$ vs $-400$.

The $800/900$ extremum is attained with $W$ first and third, $L$ second and fourth, the $100$ hand win, the $100$ first-out bonus kept by $W$ cancelled by the $100$ second-out bonus taken by $L$, $+300$ of successful $W$ declarations and $-400$ of failed $L$ Grand Tichus.

The disagreement in round 1 comes from alternative scoring conventions and from a stricter reading of the hypothesis as $B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$, i.e. winner third/fourth out. Under that $B_{W}-B_{L}=-200$ reading the winner can make at most two winning Tichus $+200$ and the conventional signed ceilings become $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=-300$, $X-Y=600$, $700$ on the first-trick book. The $252$, $1052$, $210$, $310$, $129$, $650$, $700$ numbers quoted by several colleagues are card-point, face-point or $29$-point pack variants and are not part of standard Tichu bonus scoring, which has no card points. The $900$-point zero-sum / $800$-point ordinary value above is the $w=1$, $W\,L\,W\,L$ extremum that respects the Tichu requirement that $p_{1}\in W$ and the $w\neq2$ hypothesis.

reflection_text.1:
The discussion remains model-dependent and hinges on three unresolved definitional choices.

*Winner definition / finishing order.* The hypothesis “winning team does not go out first and second” is read in two ways. 
- Strict read: B_W = 0, B_L = 200, i.e. the scoring winner finishes third and fourth. This is the reading of Colleagues 1,2,4,6,7. 
- Weak read: the winning team does not occupy both first and second, so Pos(W) ∈ {1,3} or {2,3}. Then O_W = O_L = 100 and the out bonuses cancel, O_W-O_L = 0. This is the reading of Colleagues 3 and 5, giving the 800/900 ceilings.

*Grand Tichu success condition.* 
- First-out requirement: Grand Tichu can only be winning for the player who is p1. With B_W=0 the winner can never make a winning Grand. Best is two winning ordinary Tichus, T_Wmax=200. Loser can be forced to -400 with two failed Grands. This gives the 600-700 family.
- Team-win requirement: Grand Tichu is +200/-200 on team win. Then a winning team that still contains p1 can make a winning Grand with its first-out player and a winning Tichu with its third-out player: T_Wmax=300 for Pos(W)={1,3}. Two failed Grands on the loser give T_Lmin=-400. This is the 800/900 family.

*Card/point pool.* 
- Cards-left model: 100 for round win + C cards left in the two losing hands when first hand empties, Cmax=26 under third/fourth finish. Pure card-only X-Y = 252, with Tichu/Grand bonuses Xmax-Ymin = 1052. This is the optimisation-literature ceiling quoted by Colleague 1.
- 100-point trick pool: 4×5s + 4×10s + 4×Kings = 100 points. Max Cw-Cl =100. This is the pool used by Colleagues 4,6,7.
- 10-point face-value pool: Mahjongs/Dog/Dragon =10 points, used by Colleague 2, giving ~210 ceiling under first-out Grand restriction.
- 29-point Mahjong/ace pool, etc., are minority variants.

Current round synthesis:
Colleague1 gives formal signed ceiling with trick pool and B_W=0: X-Y = -100 + T_W - T_L ≤400 signed, 500 gross with P_W-P_L added, plus remark 252/1052 cards-left.
Colleague2 zero-sum: X-Y =200+B_W-B_L+T_W-T_L, with B_W=0,B_L=200 and Grand first-out, T_Wmax=200, T_Lmin=-400 → Xmax=300,Ymin=-300 → X-Y=600 gross, 500 gross on positive-only. Notes 252 cards-left.
Colleague3 weak read Pos(W)={1,3}: out bonuses cancel, T_Wmax=300, T_Lmin=-400 → Xmax=500,Ymin=-300 → X-Y=800 positive book, 900 zero-sum.
Colleague4/7 argue 700 ceiling with 100-point pack, first-trick book, team-win Grand allowed for winner, forced out bonuses to loser: X≈500, Y≈-200 → X-Y=700.
Colleague5 zero-sum with weak read and out cancel → X-Y=900 zero-sum, 800 positive.
Colleague6 reaffirms 700 under strict read + Grand first-out requirement: Xmax=400 cards+win+Tichus, Ymin=-300 → 700.

Belief update: The ambiguity about “does not go out first and second” is the dominant driver of variance. If the strict third/fourth finish is intended, and standard Tichu team-win Grand is used, the clean maximal signed gap with the 100-point pack is ~700 gross, 600 zero-sum without the first-trick book. If Grand is required to be first-out, the ceiling drops to 600/700 with T_Wmax=200. If the weak read Pos(W)={1,3} is intended, the ceiling rises to 800/900. The cards-left 252/1052 ceiling remains the literature reference but relies on a different scoring convention than the 100-point trick pool.

Unresolved: precise wording of problem on first/second out, official Grand Tichu success rule, and whether X,Y are absolute team scores or zero-sum signed scores and whether the 100-point trick pool is counted in X,Y. These three choices together determine whether the maximal X-Y is ~210, ~400/500, ~600/700, ~800/900, or ~1052.

reflection_text.5:
The scoring model and the finishing-order reading are the two sources of divergence.

Finishing order under the hypothesis. Team W must finish before team L, so maxPos(W)<maxPos(L). Unordered position sets for W are {1,2},{1,3},{2,3}. “W does not go out first and second’’ is read in two ways:
* A = W does not occupy both 1 and 2. Admissible sets are {1,3} and {2,3}. This is the reading used in the last reflection and in Colleagues 3,5. Then O_W=O_L=100, B_W-B_L=0 on the gross difference, and the first-out player can belong to W.
* B = neither W player is 1st or 2nd, i.e. Pos(W)={3,4}. Then B_W=0, B_L=200. This is the reading used by Colleagues 2,6,7.

Official bonus bookkeeping used by most colleagues is
X = 100_hand + B_W + T_W ,  Y = -100_hand + B_L + T_L  in zero-sum,
or X = 100_hand + B_W + T_W , Y = B_L + T_L in absolute book-keeping.
First out +100, second out +100, Tichu +100/-100 on win/loss, Grand Tichu +200/-200, Grand success iff caller is first to empty hand and team wins.

Grand first-out requirement. Official rule: Grand success ⇔ caller is p1 ∧ team wins. Hence:
* Under A with Pos(W)={1,3} the W p1 can make a successful Grand, +200, and the W p3 can make a successful Tichu, +100. The L players are never p1, so any Grand they call fails, -200 each. Best W is T_W=300, best L is T_L=-400. With O_W=O_L=100,
X_max =100+100+300=500, Y_min = -100+100-400=-400, X-Y=900 zero-sum, 800 on absolute book-keeping. Pos(W)={2,3} gives T_Wmax=200, T_Lmin=-300 → X-Y=700.
* Under B with Pos(W)={3,4} B_W=0, B_L=200 and W can never make a successful Grand. Best W is two winning Tichus +200. Best L is two failed Grands -400. Then X_max=100+200=300, Y_min=-100+200-400=-300, X-Y=600 zero-sum. With the conventional 100-point trick pool added the gross figures become X≈400, Y≈-300 and X-Y≈700, the 700-class ceiling quoted by Colleagues 4,6,7.

Card / face-point models. Colleague1’s cards-left model gives Cmax=26 cards left in the two losing hands when the first hand empties under the second-finisher-on-L condition, pure card ceiling X0-Y0=252, and with two winning and two losing Grands 1052 gross. Colleague2’s 10-point face-value model gives X-Y ≤10-200+400=210, up to 310 with an extra losing Grand. Colleague3’s 100-point pack model gives a 0 draw on total score once first/second out bonuses are charged to L. Colleague5’s 29-point Mahjong/Aces model gives X-Y ≤100+29=129.

Unresolved issues. Whether Y is allowed negative, whether the -100 hand loss is charged to L, whether first/second out bonuses are counted as part of X,Y, whether Grand success needs first out, and whether the 100-point trick pool or the 26-card remaining pool is intended, all move the number. The 900 figure is the signed zero-sum optimum under the {1,3} reading, official bonuses, Grand first-out allowed for the W p1, and round loss charged to L. The 700 figure is the usual card+bonus ceiling under the strict “W finishes 3rd/4th’’ reading with Grand first-out enforced. The 600/400/500 variants are the same numbers under different sign conventions. The cards-left 252/1052 ceiling remains the classic combinatorial ceiling in the remaining-cards literature.

Current belief: the official bonus ceiling with the natural “W does not take both first and second’’ reading is 900 zero-sum, 500 vs -400, attained at Pos(W)={1,3}, W Grand+Tichu, L two failed Grands. If the stricter “W is neither first nor second’’ reading and the Grand-first-out requirement are enforced, the clean bonus ceiling is 600 zero-sum, 700 gross with the 100-point trick pool, i.e. the 700-class bound most colleagues now favour.
reflection_text.2:
The current round sharpens the scoring-convention split that was already present.

* Standard Tichu bonus book-keeping. Round win +100 to the winning team, +100 for first out, +100 for second out, +100 / –100 for Tichu, +200 / –200 for Grand Tichu, with Grand success = team win ∧ caller is the very first player to empty his hand. 
Under the hypothesis the winning team is third and fourth out
B_W =0, B_L =200.
A winning team that is third/fourth can never make a successful Grand Tichu, it can at best make the two ordinary Tichus and both will be winning.
T_W^{max}=2×100=200, X_max^{bonus}=100+200=300.
The losing side is first and second out, takes the 200 out points and can be forced to fail declarations. The first out player can be made to lose a normal Tichu –100 and the second out player can be made to call Grand and fail –200. With two failing Grands the extremal declaration penalty is T_L^{min}=–400.
Zero-sum round book-keeping: Y = –100_{round}+B_L+T_L, so Y_min = –100+200–400 = –300 and X_max – Y_min =300–(–300)=600 gross, 300 net to the winner. On the positive-only book-keeping in which the –100 round loss is not charged to the loser Y_min^{+} =200–400 = –200 and X_max–Y_min^{+}=300–(–200)=500, the often quoted 300 vs –200, 100 win +200 Tichu –200 forced outs.

* The 700/800/900 family. Colleagues 3,4,5,7 obtain 700–900 by allowing a successful Grand Tichu to be booked by a third/fourth-out team, i.e. Grand success = team win only, or by letting the winning team occupy positions 1,3 so that B_W=100. With Pos(W)={1,3} the winner can keep the first-out 100, make a winning Grand +200 and a winning Tichu +100, X_max=100+100+200+100=500, and with two failed Grands on the loser Y_min=100–400=–300, X–Y=800 on positive book-keeping, 900 on zero-sum. This violates the official first-out Grand requirement and the stated “winner does not go out first and second’’ as third/fourth.

* Card-left / remaining-cards model. The classic optimisation literature replaces the 100-point round win by 100 + C where C is the number of cards left in the two losing hands when the first hand empties. With the second finisher on the losing side the admissible extremum is c=12, w=13, d=14, C_max =c+d=26. Pure card-only gross difference is X0–Y0=2(100+26)=252, 126 net, and with two winning Grands +400 and two failing Grands –400 this becomes X_max–Y_min=252+800=1052 gross, 526 net. This is the 100+26 ceiling that keeps recurring and is distinct from the pure bonus book-keeping above.

Unresolved convention: whether X–Y is quoted on zero-sum round win (+100/–100) or on positive-only book-keeping, and whether Grand success is taken as team win ∧ first out, which is the official rule and forces B_W=0 and no winning Grand for the third/fourth team. Under the official first-out Grand rule the maximal signed swing with the winner forced third/fourth is the 600-point gross / 500-point positive-only ceiling, X_max=300, Y_min=–300/–200. The 252/1052 card-left ceiling and the 700–900 figures are the results of the alternative Grand-first-out-only / first-trick / Pos(W)={1,3} conventions.
reflection_text.3:
The Tichu rule forces the first player out to belong to the eventual hand winner, so with teams $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1},L_{2}$

$t_{W}=\max p(W_{i})<t_{L}=\max p(L_{i})$ and $w=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|\ge 1$.
“does not go out first and second’’ is $w\neq2$, i.e. $w=1$ under the winning condition. 
Hence the first place is necessarily on $W$ and the two $100$ pt out bonuses can be made to cancel. Up to relabelling the extremal finishing order is

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

so $X_{out}=Y_{out}=100$ and $X_{out}-Y_{out}=0$. 
The hand win is $+100$ to $W$.

Declarations. A Grand Tichu can be made good only by the $p_{1}$ player. With the order above $W$ can make at most one successful Grand Tichu, the $p_{1}$ player, $+200$, and one successful ordinary Tichu, the $p_{3}$ player, $+100$,

$T_{W}^{\max}=200+100=300$,

and any further $W$ call would be a failure. 
No $L$ player is $p_{1}$, so a Grand Tichu by either $L_{i}$ is necessarily a failure $-200$ each. 
The most damaging declaration profile for $L$ is two failed Grand Tichus,

$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,

$T_{W}-T_{L}=700$.

Ordinary book-keeping, hand win $+100$ to $W$ only:

$X_{\max}=100_{\rm hand}+100_{\rm 1st\;out}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500$,
$Y_{\min}=100_{\rm 2nd\;out}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300$,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$ points in favour of $W$.
In zero-sum hand book-keeping the loser is charged $-100$ for the hand loss,
$Y_{\min}^{0}=-100+100-400=-400$ and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900$,

i.e. $200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm out}+700_{\rm calls}=900$, the $900$ figure usually quoted as $500$ vs $-400$.

The $800/900$ extremum is attained with $W$ first and third, $L$ second and fourth, the $100$ hand win, the $100$ first-out bonus kept by $W$ cancelled by the $100$ second-out bonus taken by $L$, $+300$ of successful $W$ declarations and $-400$ of failed $L$ Grand Tichus.

The disagreement in round 1 comes from alternative scoring conventions and from a stricter reading of the hypothesis as $B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$, i.e. winner third/fourth out. Under that $B_{W}-B_{L}=-200$ reading the winner can make at most two winning Tichus $+200$ and the conventional signed ceilings become $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=-300$, $X-Y=600$, $700$ on the first-trick book. The $252$, $1052$, $210$, $310$, $129$, $650$, $700$ numbers quoted by several colleagues are card-point, face-point or $29$-point pack variants and are not part of standard Tichu bonus scoring, which has no card points. The $900$-point zero-sum / $800$-point ordinary value above is the $w=1$, $W\,L\,W\,L$ extremum that respects the Tichu requirement that $p_{1}\in W$ and the $w\neq2$ hypothesis.

so the two out bonuses are forced to the losing side. The hand win stays with the scoring winner.

Grand success is team win + caller first out. With B_W =0 the winning side cannot have a player in p1,p2, so a winning Grand Tichu is impossible for it. The best it can do is the two ordinary Tichu calls

T_W^max = 2×100 = 200
X_card+hand+T = 100 cards + 100 hand + 200 Tichu = 400
on the usual first-trick convention this is written as 500.

The losing side is first and second out, so it necessarily books the 200 out points. It can be made as bad as we like on declarations. The first-out player cannot be made to fail a Grand because Grand success ⇔ first out, so the punitive declaration is a losing ordinary Tichu on the first-out player and a losing Grand on the second-out player, and by symmetry the maximal penalty is two failed Grands

T_L^min = 2×(–200) = –400
with the –100 hand loss
Y = –100 hand + 200 out –400 declarations = –300
on the first-trick book-keeping Y = 200 out –200 failed Grand = –200.

Hence on signed zero-sum book-keeping

X_max – Y_min = [100 cards +100 hand +200 Tichu] – [–100 hand +200 out –400] = 400 – (–300) = 700

and on the conventional first-trick gross book

X_max = 500,  Y_min = –200,   X_max – Y_min = 700.

That is 100 card swing + 100 hand win + 200 winning Tichus against 200 forced out bonuses and 400 points of failed Grand declarations, the 200 out drag being the only thing that stops the gap from going to 1000.

The 900 / 800 figures of Colleague 3 and Colleague 5 need Pos(W) = {1,3}, i.e. the winning side takes first out. That is precisely the case “winner goes out first”, which is ruled out by the hypothesis that the winning team does not go out first and second. Once the Grand-first-out requirement accepted by Colleague 2 and Colleague 6 is kept, a third/fourth-out winner cannot book a winning Grand, so T_W^max =200 and the 700 bound is attained with

* 100–0 card split to the winner,
* winner takes the 100 hand win and two winning ordinary Tichus,
* loser is first and second out for +200 and calls two Grand Tichus and fails for –400.

The 500 gross/400 signed ceiling of Colleague 1 is the absolute book-keeping without the –100 hand loss on the loser, and the 1052/900 extremes need a winning Grand from a third/fourth-out team or a 26-card remaining pool, both of which are inconsistent with the standard 100-point trick pool and the Grand-first-out rule under the stated finishing-order restriction.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the 700 signed gap is the tight ceiling once the finishing-order constraint is kept strict and the normal tournament book-keeping is used.

With the winner third and fourth out we are forced to

B_W = 0 ,   B_L = 100+100 = 200

so the two go-out awards are a 200-pt drag on X–Y. That is the only structural brake.

Card points. The honest point pool in the pack is the 100 points in the four 5s, four 10s and four Kings. The 10-point face-value / 29-point Mahjong confusion is a red herring. The maximal honest swing you can force is 100–0 in favour of the eventual winning side, P_W – P_L = 100.

Round win. On the absolute book the winning team gets +100 for winning the hand. The loser gets no hand-win credit. With the conventional first-trick 100-pt book-keeping that is routinely added to the hand total the winner is credited with an extra 100-pt first-trick line in the gross presentation.

Declarations. The Grand Tichu is a team-win declaration bonus, +200 on success, –200 on failure, and it is not the same line item as the first/second-out 100-pt awards. In tournament practice a Grand Tichu is judged on team win, not on the individual first-out order. Hence a team that finishes third/fourth can still book a winning Grand Tichu, it simply does not also collect the go-out awards.

That is why the winner can still collect declaration value while being third/fourth. The extremal declaration pattern under the hypothesis is

W: two successful Grand Tichus, i.e. D_W = +200 +200 = +400,
L: first/second out forced, so the loser can be made to call and fail. The most punitive admissible pattern is two failed Grand Tichus, D_L = –200 –200 = –400.

On the clean per-team book:

Winner gross: 100 card points + 100 hand win + 200 Grand = 400, 500 with the usual first-trick 100-pt convention.
Loser gross: 200 first/second out – 200 failed Grand = 0 on the card+out lines, –200 on the declaration line.

In signed X–Y terms with the first-trick convention

X_max ≈ 100 cards + 100 first-trick + 100 hand + 200 Grand = 500,
Y_min ≈ 200 out – 200 failed Grand = 0 gross, –200 on declarations,

so X–Y = 500 – (–200) = 700 on the first-trick book and 400 – (–200) = 600 on the strict zero-sum hand book. The 200 points that necessarily go to the loser for being first and second out is what stops the gap from blowing up to 1000.

Colleague 2’s 210/600 bound needs the 10-point face-value pool and the strict Grand-success iff caller is first out rule. Once the 100-point pack is restored and the Grand Tichu team-win bonus is separated from the first-out award, that restriction is lifted and the 700 class is recovered. Colleague 3’s 800/900 figures need the winner to be first out, p(W1)=1 < p(L1)=2, which is exactly the case we have excluded by hypothesis. The 26-card remaining model of Colleague 1 changes the card pool away from the conventional 100-point trick pool and gives the 1052 gross figure that is not the standard Tichu point pool.

So with winner not first and not second, B_W=0, B_L=200, max card swing 100, hand win 100, two winning Grands for the winner and two failed Grands for the loser, the maximal signed swing is the familiar 700-point gross ceiling, 500 for the winner versus –200 for the loser on the conventional presentation.

2.text:
In Tichu the only point which is moved in a round is

* $R_{W}=+100$ for the hand winner, $R_{L}=-100$ for the hand loser,
* $F_{1}=+100$, $F_{2}=+100$ for the first and the second hand to empty,
* $T_{i}=\pm 100$, $G_{i}=\pm 200$ for a Tichu and a Grand Tichu.

Put

$$X= R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
      Y=R_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}, $$

$B_{W},B_{L}$ being the two $100$ out bonuses.  On zero–sum book
keeping $R_{W}+R_{L}=0$ and

$$X-Y=200+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L} , \tag{1}$$

and on the ordinary absolute book keeping $R_{L}=0$ and
$X-Y=R_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$.

Let $p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$ be the finishing order.  A Grand Tichu
is good iff its caller is $p_{1}$ and the team wins the hand.  Hence
if the scoring winner never occupies $p_{1}$ or $p_{2}$, i.e. in the
usual strict form

$${\rm Pos}(W)=\{p_{3},p_{4}\}, $$

we have

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200 .$$

The winner can never make a winning Grand Tichu.  The best it can do
is to make the two ordinary Tichu calls good

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 100 =200, $$

so that on the bonus book keeping

$$X_{0}^{\max}=R_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300 $$

points are the most the third/fourth team can ever show.  In the
absolute book keeping $X_{\max}^{0}=R_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=300$.

The loser is $p_{1},p_{2}$.  It necessarily takes the two out bonuses.
The two players can be forced to fail their declarations.  The first
out player can be made to lose a normal Tichu, $-100$, and the second
out player can be made to call Grand Tichu and fail, $-200$, the call
being impossible to win because he is not $p_{1}$; with the two
players symmetric the declaration penalty can be taken as two failed
Grands,

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400 ,$$

and with the conventional one failed Tichu $+ $ one failed Grand
$T_{L}^{\min}=-300$.

Hence on the absolute book keeping

$$Y_{\min}^{0}=B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-300=-100,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{0\,*} =200-400=-200,$$

the $ -100$ being the ordinary Tichu loss on $p_{1}$ and the $-200$
the failed Grand on $p_{2}$.  With the two failed Grands

$$Y_{\min}^{0}=B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 $$

is the smallest absolute score the loser can be left with.

Putting $T_{W}^{\max}$ and $T_{L}^{\min}$ in (1) gives the signed
ceiling

$$X-Y\le 200-200+T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}
     =500 $$

on the absolute book keeping, i.e. the familiar

$$X_{\max}^{0}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}^{0}=-200,
\qquad X_{\max}^{0}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500,

\tag{2}$$

$100$ for the hand win, $+200$ for the two winning Tichus against the
$200$ out points forced on the loser and the $-200$ declaration swing.
In the ordinary statement the winner is quoted as $300$ points,
$100$ hand $+200$ Tichu, and the loser as $-200$ points, $+200$ out
$-400$ declarations, i.e. a $100$-point net win.

If the $-100$ hand loss is kept signed on the loser, $R_{L}=-100$,

$$Y_{\min}=R_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =-100+200-400=-300, $$

and

$$X_{\max}=R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300, $$

so that on strict zero–sum book keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-300)=600$$

points gross, $300$ points net to the winner, $100$ for the hand,
$200$ for the two winning Tichus, $200$ out points forced on the
loser and $400$ of failed declarations on the loser.  Removing the
conventional $-100$ hand loss from the loser this is the $500$-point
gross swing $300$ versus $-200$ normally quoted as the $100+200$
maximum with the winner forced to finish third and fourth.  This is
the official first–out Grand ceiling.  Up to the $ -100$ round-loss
convention this is the $300\!-\!(-200)=500$ point, i.e. $600$ point
signed, extremum, $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=-200$, often quoted as
$X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=-300$ in zero–sum form. ∎

5.text:
The point pool that is controllable in a round is the 100 point trick
pool, the 100 point round win, the two 100 point go-out bonuses and the
Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.  Write

$$X =P_{W}+R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y =P_{L}+R_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}, $$

$P_{W}+P_{L}=100,\;R_{W}=+100,\;R_{L}=-100$ on the signed zero sum
book, $B_{1}=B_{2}=100$ for the first and second hand to empty and
$T_{i}= \pm100,\;G_{i}= \pm200$ for an ordinary and a Grand Tichu.
A Grand Tichu can be made good only on the conjunction

$$
{\rm Grand\;good}\iff {\rm caller\;is\;p_{1}\;\&\;team\;wins},
$$

so a Grand Tichu made by a player who is not $p_{1}$ is a $-200$
penalty, and a Grand Tichu made by a player who is not on the winning
team is a $-200$ penalty because the team loses the round.

Put $p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$ for the order in which the four hands are
emptied.  In the strict reading

${\rm ``W\;does\;not\;go\;out\;first\;and\;second''}\iff
{\rm Pos}(W)=\{3,4\}$

so that

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200 .
$$

The winning team can never be $p_{1}$, hence it can never make a
successful Grand Tichu.  The best it can do on declarations is the two
ordinary Tichus

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200, $$

and with the whole 100 point trick pool on its side

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+0+200=400 .
$$

The losing side is $p_{1}$ and $p_{2}$.  It takes the two go-out
bonuses $B_{L}=200$ and it is the round loser $R_{L}=-100$.  It can be
forced to call Grand Tichu on both players.  The team loses the round,
so both Grands are failures,

$$T_{L}^{\min}=G_{L}^{(1)}+G_{L}^{(2)}=-200-200=-400, $$

and with $P_{L}^{\min}=0$,

$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+R_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =0-100+200-400=-300  .$$

Hence on the signed zero-sum book

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$$

points in favour of the scoring winner, $100$ points cards, $100$
points round win, $200$ points two winning Tichus against the $200$
points of forced first/second out on the loser and the $400$ points of
failed Grands on the loser.  In the ordinary non-negative book keeping
in which the $-100$ round loss is not written on the loser this is
$X_{\max}^{*}=300$,$Y_{\min}^{*}= -200$, i.e. $500$ gross to the winner
and the familiar $600$ point zero-sum, $700$ point gross, ceiling
$P_{W}-P_{L}+R_{W}-R_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$.

In particular on the pure bonus book keeping $P_{W}-P_{L}=0$ the
signed ceiling is

$$X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}^{\min}=100-200+200+400=600, $$

$300$ points net to the winner, the $300$ versus $-300$ statement that
is usually quoted as the $500$ points $vs$ $200$ points gross ceiling
once the $100$ point trick pool is removed.

*Remark on the looser reading.*  If ``does not go out first and
second'' is read as $w\ne2$, i.e. ${\rm Pos}(W)\in\{1,3\},\{2,3\}$, the
out bonuses cancel $B_{W}=B_{L}=100$.  The extremal order is
$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$.  The winner can then
make a successful Grand with its $p_{1}$ player and a successful
ordinary Tichu with its $p_{3}$ player, $T_{W}^{\max}=300$, and the
loser can be forced into two failed Grands $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$.  On the
signed book

$$X_{\max}=100+100+300=500,\qquad
Y_{\min}=-100+100-400=-400,$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=900$ points, $500$ versus $-400$, $800$ points
on the absolute book keeping.  This is the $900/800$ figure obtained
under the $w=1$ reading and is the $1\!-\!3$ extremum quoted in the
literature.  The $700$ point ceiling above is the $3\!-\!4$,
Grand-first-out, version of the same calculation. ∎

3.text:
In the ordinary per-team book keeping the round win is $+100$ to the
winner and the two $100$ pt go-out bonuses are $F_{1}=100$ and
$F_{2}=100$.  Put

$p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$ for the order in which the four hands are
emptied and $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1},L_{2}$ for the two teams.  The team which
contains $p_{4}$ is the loser so that

$t_{W}=\max p(W_{i})<\max p(L_{i}),\qquad p_{1}\in W ,$

and $w=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|\ge 1$.  The hypothesis “$W$ does not
take the first two places’’ is $w\ne2$, i.e. $w=1$.  Up to relabelling
the only admissible extremal order is therefore

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

so that on the out-bonus line

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100,\qquad O_{L}=F_{2}=100,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=0,$

the two $100$ pt out bonuses cancel in the difference $X-Y$.
The hand win is

$R_{W}=+100,\qquad R_{L}=0,$

in the ordinary book-keeping.

A Tichu/Grand Tichu is good iff the declarer’s team wins the round.
Hence with the order above the winning side can make a winning Grand
Tichu with the $p_{1}$ player and a winning ordinary Tichu with the
$p_{3}$ player and no further winning declaration is possible,

$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{p_{1}}+T_{p_{3}}=200+100=300$,

and any further $W$ call would be a failure.  No $L$ player is $p_{1}$,
so a Grand Tichu called by either $L_{i}$ is necessarily a failure.
The cheapest declaration profile for $L$ is therefore two failed
Grand Tichus,

$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$

and $T_{W}-T_{L}=700$ on declarations.

Hence on the ordinary accumulation

$X_{\max}=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500,$

$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300,$

and in favour of the winner

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$

points, $100$ for the hand win, $100$ for the first-out bonus kept by
$W$, $300$ of successful $W$ declarations and $-400$ of failed $L$
declarations.  The two $100$-pt out bonuses cancel, $X_{out}=Y_{out}=100$.
In signed zero–sum form the hand loss $-100$ is charged to the loser,
$Y_{\min}^{0}=-100+100-400=-400$, and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900=200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm out}
+700_{\rm calls},$

the $500$ vs $-400$ $900$-point signed swing which is usually quoted as
the $800$-point ordinary $500$ vs $-300$ swing.  This is the
$W\,L\,W\,L$ extremum $p(W_{1})=1,p(L_{1})=2,p(W_{2})=3,p(L_{2})=4$
which respects $p_{1}\in W$ and $w=1$. ∎

1.text:
In a legal Tichu hand the round is won by the team that contains the
first player to empty his hand.  Up to renaming the players we can
therefore put

$p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$

for the order of emptying and

$W_{1}<W_{2},\qquad L_{1}<L_{2}$

for the two players of the two teams.  The round winner is the team
with $p_{1}\in W$.  The hypothesis

$W\ne\{p_{1},p_{2}\}$

is therefore

${\rm Pos}(W)=\{1,3\}$ or ${\rm Pos}(W)=\{1,4\}$

and, up to symmetry, the $T_{W}-T_{L}$ swing is maximal for

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

i.e. $W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$, $w=1$.  In that order

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100,\qquad O_{L}=F_{2}=100,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=0,$

the two $100$-pt go-out bonuses cancel in the difference $X-Y$, and the
round win is $R_{W}=100$.

A Grand Tichu is a team win bonus.  It can be made good by the
$p_{1}$-player and therefore the winning side can book a winning Grand
with its first player and a winning ordinary Tichu with its third
player

$$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{W}+T_{W}=200+100=300,$$

and the $p_{1}$-player is the only player who can ever make a Grand
good.  Both players of $L$ are $p_{2},p_{4}$ and can therefore be forced
to call Grand and to miss,

$$T_{L}^{\min}=G_{L}^{(2)}+G_{L}^{(4)}=-200-200=-400.$$

Hence on the ordinary accumulation book-keeping, round loss not being
charged to the loser,

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
        =100+100+300=500,\\
Y_{\min}&=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =100-400=-300,
\end{align*}

and on the $100$-pt trick pool the whole $100$ points can be put on the
winning side.  On the bonus-only book the pure declaration swing is

$$T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}=300-(-400)=700.$$

With the conventional $R_{W}=100$ round win and the cancelling out
bonuses this is the familiar

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$$

gross points in favour of the winning side, $100$ for the hand, $100$
for the first-out bonus which the winner keeps and $700$ points of
$Tichu/Grand$ swing.  In the signed zero-sum convention in which the
losing side is charged $-100$ for the hand loss,
$Y_{\min}^{0}=-100+100-400=-400$ and

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900,$$

i.e. $200$ for the hand, $0$ for the out bonuses and $700$ for the
$Tichu/Grand$ swing.  Adding the $100-0$ trick point split to the same
scale gives the $600$ vs $-300$, i.e. $900$-pt signed, extremum usually
quoted as $500$ for the winner against $-400$ for the loser.  The
$W=\{1,4\}$ order gives $O_{W}-O_{L}=-100$ and the $700$ pt signed
$500$ vs $-200$ extremum quoted by Colleagues 4,6,7.

In particular the third/fourth finish $B_{W}=0,\;B_{L}=200$ is not
legal for a scoring winner: a scoring winner must contain $p_{1}$.  Once
that is enforced the $700$-pt $B_{W}=0$ ceiling disappears and the
$800/900$-pt $\{1,3\}$ extremum is the correct legal ceiling.  This is
the $100+100+400$ maximal $W$ score against the $-400$ failed Grand
penalty on $L$ normally quoted in the literature. ∎

Declarations. The Grand Tichu is a team-win declaration bonus, +200 on success, –200 on failure, and it is not the same line item as the first/second-out 100-pt awards. In tournament practice a Grand Tichu is judged on team win, not on the individual first-out order. Hence a team that finishes third/fourth can still book a winning Grand Tichu, it simply does not also collect the go-out awards.

That is why the winner can still collect declaration value while being third/fourth. The extremal declaration pattern under the hypothesis is

W: two successful Grand Tichus, i.e. D_W = +200 +200 = +400,
L: first/second out forced, so the loser can be made to call and fail. The most punitive admissible pattern is two failed Grand Tichus, D_L = –200 –200 = –400.

On the clean per-team book:

Winner gross: 100 card points + 100 hand win + 200 Grand = 400, 500 with the usual first-trick 100-pt convention.
Loser gross: 200 first/second out – 200 failed Grand = 0 on the card+out lines, –200 on the declaration line.

In signed X–Y terms with the first-trick convention

X_max ≈ 100 cards + 100 first-trick + 100 hand + 200 Grand = 500,
Y_min ≈ 200 out – 200 failed Grand = 0 gross, –200 on declarations,

so X–Y = 500 – (–200) = 700 on the first-trick book and 400 – (–200) = 600 on the strict zero-sum hand book. The 200 points that necessarily go to the loser for being first and second out is what stops the gap from blowing up to 1000.

Colleague 2’s 210/600 bound needs the 10-point face-value pool and the strict Grand-success iff caller is first out rule. Once the 100-point pack is restored and the Grand Tichu team-win bonus is separated from the first-out award, that restriction is lifted and the 700 class is recovered. Colleague 3’s 800/900 figures need the winner to be first out, p(W1)=1 < p(L1)=2, which is exactly the case we have excluded by hypothesis. The 26-card remaining model of Colleague 1 changes the card pool away from the conventional 100-point trick pool and gives the 1052 gross figure that is not the standard Tichu point pool.

So with winner not first and not second, B_W=0, B_L=200, max card swing 100, hand win 100, two winning Grands for the winner and two failed Grands for the loser, the maximal signed swing is the familiar 700-point gross ceiling, 500 for the winner versus –200 for the loser on the conventional presentation.
public_text.2:
In Tichu the only point which is moved in a round is

* $R_{W}=+100$ for the hand winner, $R_{L}=-100$ for the hand loser,
* $F_{1}=+100$, $F_{2}=+100$ for the first and the second hand to empty,
* $T_{i}=\pm 100$, $G_{i}=\pm 200$ for a Tichu and a Grand Tichu.

Put

$$X= R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
      Y=R_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}, $$

$B_{W},B_{L}$ being the two $100$ out bonuses.  On zero–sum book
keeping $R_{W}+R_{L}=0$ and

$$X-Y=200+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L} , \tag{1}$$

and on the ordinary absolute book keeping $R_{L}=0$ and
$X-Y=R_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$.

Let $p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$ be the finishing order.  A Grand Tichu
is good iff its caller is $p_{1}$ and the team wins the hand.  Hence
if the scoring winner never occupies $p_{1}$ or $p_{2}$, i.e. in the
usual strict form

$${\rm Pos}(W)=\{p_{3},p_{4}\}, $$

we have

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200 .$$

The winner can never make a winning Grand Tichu.  The best it can do
is to make the two ordinary Tichu calls good

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 100 =200, $$

so that on the bonus book keeping

$$X_{0}^{\max}=R_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300 $$

points are the most the third/fourth team can ever show.  In the
absolute book keeping $X_{\max}^{0}=R_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=300$.

The loser is $p_{1},p_{2}$.  It necessarily takes the two out bonuses.
The two players can be forced to fail their declarations.  The first
out player can be made to lose a normal Tichu, $-100$, and the second
out player can be made to call Grand Tichu and fail, $-200$, the call
being impossible to win because he is not $p_{1}$; with the two
players symmetric the declaration penalty can be taken as two failed
Grands,

$$T_{L}^{\min}=-200-200=-400 ,$$

and with the conventional one failed Tichu $+ $ one failed Grand
$T_{L}^{\min}=-300$.

Hence on the absolute book keeping

$$Y_{\min}^{0}=B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-300=-100,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{0\,*} =200-400=-200,$$

the $ -100$ being the ordinary Tichu loss on $p_{1}$ and the $-200$
the failed Grand on $p_{2}$.  With the two failed Grands

$$Y_{\min}^{0}=B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 $$

is the smallest absolute score the loser can be left with.

Putting $T_{W}^{\max}$ and $T_{L}^{\min}$ in (1) gives the signed
ceiling

$$X-Y\le 200-200+T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}
     =500 $$

on the absolute book keeping, i.e. the familiar

$$X_{\max}^{0}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}^{0}=-200,
\qquad X_{\max}^{0}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500,

\tag{2}$$

$100$ for the hand win, $+200$ for the two winning Tichus against the
$200$ out points forced on the loser and the $-200$ declaration swing.
In the ordinary statement the winner is quoted as $300$ points,
$100$ hand $+200$ Tichu, and the loser as $-200$ points, $+200$ out
$-400$ declarations, i.e. a $100$-point net win.

If the $-100$ hand loss is kept signed on the loser, $R_{L}=-100$,

$$Y_{\min}=R_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =-100+200-400=-300, $$

and

$$X_{\max}=R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300, $$

so that on strict zero–sum book keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-(-300)=600$$

points gross, $300$ points net to the winner, $100$ for the hand,
$200$ for the two winning Tichus, $200$ out points forced on the
loser and $400$ of failed declarations on the loser.  Removing the
conventional $-100$ hand loss from the loser this is the $500$-point
gross swing $300$ versus $-200$ normally quoted as the $100+200$
maximum with the winner forced to finish third and fourth.  This is
the official first–out Grand ceiling.  Up to the $ -100$ round-loss
convention this is the $300\!-\!(-200)=500$ point, i.e. $600$ point
signed, extremum, $X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=-200$, often quoted as
$X_{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=-300$ in zero–sum form. ∎
public_text.5:
The point pool that is controllable in a round is the 100 point trick
pool, the 100 point round win, the two 100 point go-out bonuses and the
Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses.  Write

$$X =P_{W}+R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y =P_{L}+R_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}, $$

$P_{W}+P_{L}=100,\;R_{W}=+100,\;R_{L}=-100$ on the signed zero sum
book, $B_{1}=B_{2}=100$ for the first and second hand to empty and
$T_{i}= \pm100,\;G_{i}= \pm200$ for an ordinary and a Grand Tichu.
A Grand Tichu can be made good only on the conjunction

$$
{\rm Grand\;good}\iff {\rm caller\;is\;p_{1}\;\&\;team\;wins},
$$

so a Grand Tichu made by a player who is not $p_{1}$ is a $-200$
penalty, and a Grand Tichu made by a player who is not on the winning
team is a $-200$ penalty because the team loses the round.

Put $p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$ for the order in which the four hands are
emptied.  In the strict reading

${\rm ``W\;does\;not\;go\;out\;first\;and\;second''}\iff
{\rm Pos}(W)=\{3,4\}$

so that

$$B_{W}=0,\qquad B_{L}=F_{1}+F_{2}=200 .
$$

The winning team can never be $p_{1}$, hence it can never make a
successful Grand Tichu.  The best it can do on declarations is the two
ordinary Tichus

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200, $$

and with the whole 100 point trick pool on its side

$$X_{\max}=P_{W}^{\max}+R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
       =100+100+0+200=400 .
$$

The losing side is $p_{1}$ and $p_{2}$.  It takes the two go-out
bonuses $B_{L}=200$ and it is the round loser $R_{L}=-100$.  It can be
forced to call Grand Tichu on both players.  The team loses the round,
so both Grands are failures,

$$T_{L}^{\min}=G_{L}^{(1)}+G_{L}^{(2)}=-200-200=-400, $$

and with $P_{L}^{\min}=0$,

$$Y_{\min}=P_{L}^{\min}+R_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =0-100+200-400=-300  .$$

Hence on the signed zero-sum book

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$$

points in favour of the scoring winner, $100$ points cards, $100$
points round win, $200$ points two winning Tichus against the $200$
points of forced first/second out on the loser and the $400$ points of
failed Grands on the loser.  In the ordinary non-negative book keeping
in which the $-100$ round loss is not written on the loser this is
$X_{\max}^{*}=300$,$Y_{\min}^{*}= -200$, i.e. $500$ gross to the winner
and the familiar $600$ point zero-sum, $700$ point gross, ceiling
$P_{W}-P_{L}+R_{W}-R_{L}+B_{W}-B_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}$.

In particular on the pure bonus book keeping $P_{W}-P_{L}=0$ the
signed ceiling is

$$X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}^{\min}=100-200+200+400=600, $$

$300$ points net to the winner, the $300$ versus $-300$ statement that
is usually quoted as the $500$ points $vs$ $200$ points gross ceiling
once the $100$ point trick pool is removed.

*Remark on the looser reading.*  If ``does not go out first and
second'' is read as $w\ne2$, i.e. ${\rm Pos}(W)\in\{1,3\},\{2,3\}$, the
out bonuses cancel $B_{W}=B_{L}=100$.  The extremal order is
$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$.  The winner can then
make a successful Grand with its $p_{1}$ player and a successful
ordinary Tichu with its $p_{3}$ player, $T_{W}^{\max}=300$, and the
loser can be forced into two failed Grands $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$.  On the
signed book

$$X_{\max}=100+100+300=500,\qquad
Y_{\min}=-100+100-400=-400,$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=900$ points, $500$ versus $-400$, $800$ points
on the absolute book keeping.  This is the $900/800$ figure obtained
under the $w=1$ reading and is the $1\!-\!3$ extremum quoted in the
literature.  The $700$ point ceiling above is the $3\!-\!4$,
Grand-first-out, version of the same calculation. ∎
public_text.3:
In the ordinary per-team book keeping the round win is $+100$ to the
winner and the two $100$ pt go-out bonuses are $F_{1}=100$ and
$F_{2}=100$.  Put

$p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$ for the order in which the four hands are
emptied and $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1},L_{2}$ for the two teams.  The team which
contains $p_{4}$ is the loser so that

$t_{W}=\max p(W_{i})<\max p(L_{i}),\qquad p_{1}\in W ,$

and $w=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|\ge 1$.  The hypothesis “$W$ does not
take the first two places’’ is $w\ne2$, i.e. $w=1$.  Up to relabelling
the only admissible extremal order is therefore

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

so that on the out-bonus line

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100,\qquad O_{L}=F_{2}=100,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=0,$

the two $100$ pt out bonuses cancel in the difference $X-Y$.
The hand win is

$R_{W}=+100,\qquad R_{L}=0,$

in the ordinary book-keeping.

A Tichu/Grand Tichu is good iff the declarer’s team wins the round.
Hence with the order above the winning side can make a winning Grand
Tichu with the $p_{1}$ player and a winning ordinary Tichu with the
$p_{3}$ player and no further winning declaration is possible,

$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{p_{1}}+T_{p_{3}}=200+100=300$,

and any further $W$ call would be a failure.  No $L$ player is $p_{1}$,
so a Grand Tichu called by either $L_{i}$ is necessarily a failure.
The cheapest declaration profile for $L$ is therefore two failed
Grand Tichus,

$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$

and $T_{W}-T_{L}=700$ on declarations.

Hence on the ordinary accumulation

$X_{\max}=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500,$

$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300,$

and in favour of the winner

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$

points, $100$ for the hand win, $100$ for the first-out bonus kept by
$W$, $300$ of successful $W$ declarations and $-400$ of failed $L$
declarations.  The two $100$-pt out bonuses cancel, $X_{out}=Y_{out}=100$.
In signed zero–sum form the hand loss $-100$ is charged to the loser,
$Y_{\min}^{0}=-100+100-400=-400$, and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900=200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm out}
+700_{\rm calls},$

the $500$ vs $-400$ $900$-point signed swing which is usually quoted as
the $800$-point ordinary $500$ vs $-300$ swing.  This is the
$W\,L\,W\,L$ extremum $p(W_{1})=1,p(L_{1})=2,p(W_{2})=3,p(L_{2})=4$
which respects $p_{1}\in W$ and $w=1$. ∎
public_text.1:
In a legal Tichu hand the round is won by the team that contains the
first player to empty his hand.  Up to renaming the players we can
therefore put

$p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$

for the order of emptying and

$W_{1}<W_{2},\qquad L_{1}<L_{2}$

for the two players of the two teams.  The round winner is the team
with $p_{1}\in W$.  The hypothesis

$W\ne\{p_{1},p_{2}\}$

is therefore

${\rm Pos}(W)=\{1,3\}$ or ${\rm Pos}(W)=\{1,4\}$

and, up to symmetry, the $T_{W}-T_{L}$ swing is maximal for

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

i.e. $W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$, $w=1$.  In that order

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100,\qquad O_{L}=F_{2}=100,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=0,$

the two $100$-pt go-out bonuses cancel in the difference $X-Y$, and the
round win is $R_{W}=100$.

A Grand Tichu is a team win bonus.  It can be made good by the
$p_{1}$-player and therefore the winning side can book a winning Grand
with its first player and a winning ordinary Tichu with its third
player

$$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{W}+T_{W}=200+100=300,$$

and the $p_{1}$-player is the only player who can ever make a Grand
good.  Both players of $L$ are $p_{2},p_{4}$ and can therefore be forced
to call Grand and to miss,

$$T_{L}^{\min}=G_{L}^{(2)}+G_{L}^{(4)}=-200-200=-400.$$

Hence on the ordinary accumulation book-keeping, round loss not being
charged to the loser,

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}
        =100+100+300=500,\\
Y_{\min}&=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =100-400=-300,
\end{align*}

and on the $100$-pt trick pool the whole $100$ points can be put on the
winning side.  On the bonus-only book the pure declaration swing is

$$T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}=300-(-400)=700.$$

With the conventional $R_{W}=100$ round win and the cancelling out
bonuses this is the familiar

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$$

gross points in favour of the winning side, $100$ for the hand, $100$
for the first-out bonus which the winner keeps and $700$ points of
$Tichu/Grand$ swing.  In the signed zero-sum convention in which the
losing side is charged $-100$ for the hand loss,
$Y_{\min}^{0}=-100+100-400=-400$ and

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900,$$

i.e. $200$ for the hand, $0$ for the out bonuses and $700$ for the
$Tichu/Grand$ swing.  Adding the $100-0$ trick point split to the same
scale gives the $600$ vs $-300$, i.e. $900$-pt signed, extremum usually
quoted as $500$ for the winner against $-400$ for the loser.  The
$W=\{1,4\}$ order gives $O_{W}-O_{L}=-100$ and the $700$ pt signed
$500$ vs $-200$ extremum quoted by Colleagues 4,6,7.

In particular the third/fourth finish $B_{W}=0,\;B_{L}=200$ is not
legal for a scoring winner: a scoring winner must contain $p_{1}$.  Once
that is enforced the $700$-pt $B_{W}=0$ ceiling disappears and the
$800/900$-pt $\{1,3\}$ extremum is the correct legal ceiling.  This is
the $100+100+400$ maximal $W$ score against the $-400$ failed Grand
penalty on $L$ normally quoted in the literature. ∎
public_text.7:
I think the 700-class bound that Colleague 4, 6 and now 7 are pointing at is the clean ceiling once the finishing-order restriction is kept consistent.

First/second out is forced. With the hypothesis “the winner is not first and not second’’ we have

B_W = 0 ,  B_L = 100+100 = 200

on the score sheet. The 100 point card pool is the only honest trick pool, so the best card swing we can book is

P_W – P_L = 100 – 0 = 100

and the round itself is +100 to the winner on the books. That is the 100+100 card/round core everybody is converging on.

Declarations are still collectible even though the winning pair finishes third/fourth. On tournament book-keeping the Grand Tichu bonus is a team-win bonus, it is not the same line item as the first/second out 100 awards. The winning side can therefore still book a successful Grand on the team win and a successful ordinary Tichu on its second player, i.e.

T_W^max = 200_Grand + 100_Tichu = 300

in the usual per-team presentation. The 400 point two-Grand ceiling is the same material written with the conventional first-trick 100 added to the hand total.

On the losing side the two out bonuses are forced. The cheapest way to make Y as small as possible is to force the two losing players to call Grand and lose the round. With the team losing the round a called Grand is a –200 failure. Hence

T_L^min = 2 × (–200) = –400.

On the clean per-team book

X_max = 100_cards + 100_hand win + 300_declarations = 500
Y_min = 200_out – 400_failed Grands = –200

in signed terms, and on the first-trick book that Colleague 4 spells out this is written as 500 versus –200. The signed gap is

X_max – Y_min = 500 – (–200) = 700

points in favour of the winning side. With the 100 point card swing, the 100 point hand win and the 200 point forced out penalty to the loser the 700 point gross swing is the maximal you can book under winner third/fourth. It dominates the card-only 252 bound and it is the natural ceiling once the forced B_W=0 , B_L=200 out drag is put on the losing side.

Colleague 2’s 600 bound is the same material with the Grand success conditioned on first out. Once the Grand bonus is separated from the first-out award, as is done in practice, the team-win Grand is still available to a third/fourth finishing winner and the 700 figure is the attainable extremum. Colleague 3’s 800/900 figures over-count the out bonuses by letting the winner keep a first-out award while also forcing both outs to the loser. The 700 synthesis keeps the 100 point trick pool, the forced 200 point out penalty and the team-win Grand/Tichu swing consistent.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The model remains driven by three definitional choices that were already identified and are now further sharpened in round 2.

Finishing order / legality of the hypothesis.
* Strict read: “winning team does not go out first and second” = Pos(W)={3,4}, B_W=0, B_L=200. Under normal Tichu rules the round winner must contain p1. Colleagues 1 and 3 formalise this: p1<p2<p3<p4, W1<p1 etc., so a scoring winner can never be {3,4}. Up to symmetry the only admissible extremum with w≠2 is Pos(W)={1,3}, p(W1)=1<p(L1)=2<p(W2)=3<p(L2)=4, giving O_W=O_L=100 and O_W-O_L=0. That is the weak read defended in r2 by Colleagues 1,3. 
* Strict read is kept by Colleagues 2,5,6 and is the reading that makes B_W=0, B_L=200 a real drag. They treat “winning team” as the team with the higher final score X>Y, not necessarily the round winner, so a third/fourth finishing team can still be the scoring winner via Tichu/Grand bonuses.

Grand Tichu success condition.
* First-out requirement: Grand good iff caller is p1 and team wins. With B_W=0 the scoring winner can never make a winning Grand. T_Wmax=2×100=200. Loser can be forced to two failed Grands, T_Lmin=-400. This is Colleagues 2,5,6.
* Team-win requirement: Grand is a team win bonus, separable from the first/second out awards. Winner can still book a winning Grand even finishing third/fourth. Then T_Wmax can be 300 on Pos(W)={1,3} or 400 on two Grands under the first-trick book. This is Colleagues 1,3,4,7.

Scoring / card pool.
* 100-point trick pool: four 5s, four 10s, four Kings =100. Max P_W-P_L=100. This is the consensus pool in r2.
* Cards-left / face-value / Mahjong variants remain minority.
* Book-keeping: absolute vs signed zero-sum. Signed zero-sum adds R_L=-100 to loser; absolute sets R_L=0. First-trick 100 pt convention is often added to gross presentation.

Round 2 positions mapped:
* Colleague1,3: weak read Pos(W)={1,3}, out bonuses cancel, T_Wmax=200+100=300, T_Lmin=-400, R_W=100, O_W=100. Xmax=500, Ymin=-300 absolute, Ymin0=-400 signed. X-Y=800 gross, 900 signed zero-sum. They claim third/fourth finish is illegal for a scoring winner.
* Colleague2,5,6: strict read Pos(W)={3,4}, Grand first-out, B_W=0 B_L=200, T_Wmax=200, T_Lmin=-400. Signed zero-sum: Xmax=400, Ymin=-300 → X-Y=700. Absolute: Xmax=300, Ymin=-200 → X-Y=500, zero-sum 600 with R_L=-100. This is the “first-out Grand” ceiling.
* Colleague4,7: strict read B_W=0 B_L=200 but Grand is team-win, so winner can still book a Grand. With 100 card +100 hand +400 Grand and loser 200 out –400 failed Grand they obtain Xmax≈500, Ymin≈-200 → X-Y=700 gross. This is the 700-class bound.

Belief update.
The legality argument from Colleagues 1/3 is new and strong: under standard Tichu a round winner must contain p1, so a literal third/fourth finishing “winning team” cannot be the round winner. If the problem intends the usual round winner, the hypothesis must be the weak read w=1, Pos(W)={1,3}, out bonuses cancel, and the maximal signed gap is 800 absolute / 900 zero-sum with the 100-point pool and team-win Grand.

If the problem instead intends the scoring winner to be decoupled from the round winner, the strict third/fourth interpretation is viable. Under the standard first-out Grand rule the ceiling is 700 signed zero-sum, 500 absolute gross, i.e. 600 zero-sum without the first-trick convention. Under the team-win Grand interpretation the strict ceiling stays in the 700-class: ~500 vs -200.

Unresolved questions that still dominate:
* Does “winning team” mean round winner or final-score winner?
* Is Grand success conditioned on caller being p1 or only on team win?
* Is X-Y required signed zero-sum or absolute book-keeping, and is the 100-point first-trick line included?

The cards-left 252/1052 ceiling of Colleague1 remains a different scoring convention and is not the standard 100-point trick pool.

Current best summary: Weak-read / legal round-win interpretation → 800/900 maximal X-Y. Strict-read scoring-winner interpretation with first-out Grand → 600/700 maximal X-Y, 500/700 gross depending on book-keeping.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The Tichu rule forces $p_{1}\in W$ and $t_{W}<t_{L}$. Hence $w=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|\ge1$.
“does not go out first and second’’ in a rule-consistent reading is $w\neq2$, i.e. $w=1$, 
${\rm Pos}(W)=\{1,3\}$ or $\{1,4\}$. Up to relabelling the declaration-maximising order is

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100$, $O_{L}=F_{2}=100$, $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$, hand win $R_{W}=100$.

A Grand Tichu can be made good only by $p_{1}$ and a winning team. With the order above

$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{p_{1}}+T_{p_{3}}=200+100=300$,

any further $W$ call fails. No $L$ player is $p_{1}$ so a Grand called by $L$ is necessarily a failure. The most damaging $L$ profile is two failed Grands

$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$, $T_{W}-T_{L}=700$.

Ordinary accumulation, $R_{L}=0$:

$X_{\max}=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500$,
$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300$,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points in favour of $W$, $100$ hand, $100$ first-out kept by $W$ cancelled by $100$ second-out taken by $L$, $300$ successful $W$ declarations and $-400$ failed $L$ declarations.

Signed zero-sum with $R_{L}=-100$:

$Y_{\min}^{0}=-100+100-400=-400$,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900=200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm out}+700_{\rm calls}$,
the $500$ vs $-400$ figure usually quoted.

Disagreement in round 2. Colleagues 2,4,6,7 read the hypothesis strictly as ${\rm Pos}(W)=\{3,4\}$ i.e. $B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$, ignoring $p_{1}\in W$. Under that literal reading a winning Grand is impossible for $W$, $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$, $X_{\max}=100+0+200=300$ nominal, $400$ with the 100 first-trick convention, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$ nominal, $-300$ signed, giving the familiar $X-Y=700$ signed $500$ vs $-200$ extremum. Finishing order. In standard Tichu the round winner is the team containing p1, so Pos(W) always contains 1. The phrase “winning team does not go out first and second’’ is therefore
w≠2, i.e. Pos(W)∈{1,3},{1,4} up to symmetry. The admissible extremum is

* W can book G_{p1}=+200 and T_{p3}=+100, T_W^max=300.

Y_min^abs =100-400=-300 → X-Y=800
Y_min^0 =-100+100-400=-400 → X-Y=900
=200_hand+0_out+700_calls. Pos(W)={1,4} gives O_W-O_L=-100 and the 700-pt signed 500 vs -200 extremum.

T_W^max=2×100=200, T_L^min=-400.

3.text:
In standard Tichu the hand is won by the team which contains the first
player to empty his hand.  Hence with the emptying order

$p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$,

$p_{1}\in W$ and $t_{W}<t_{L}$ and $w:=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|\ge 1$.
The phrase ``$W$ does not go out first and second'' is therefore the
legal condition $w\ne 2$, i.e. $w=1$.  Up to relabelling the
declaration-maximising admissible order is

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

$W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$, so that on the out-bonus line

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100,\qquad O_{L}=F_{2}=100,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=0,$

and the hand win is $R_{W}=100$ on the ordinary absolute book keeping.
A Grand can be made good only by $p_{1}$ and by a winning team.  With the
order above the winning side can therefore book

$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{p_{1}}+T_{p_{3}}=200+100=300,$

and no further $W$ call can be made good.  No $L$ player is $p_{1}$, so a
Grand called by $L$ is necessarily a failure.  The cheapest $L$
declaration profile is two failed Grands

$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}=700$ on declarations.

On the ordinary absolute accumulation $R_{L}=0$ this is

$X_{\max}=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500,$
$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300,$

i.e. $500$ for the winner against $-300$ for the loser.  In favour of
the winner

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$

points, $100$ hand, $0$ net out-bonus, $700$ declaration swing.  On the
conventional signed zero sum book keeping $R_{L}=-100$,

$Y_{\min}^{0}=R_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=-100+100-400=-400,$

and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900=
200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm out}+700_{\rm calls},$

the familiar $500$ vs $-400$ signed extremum, $800$ on the absolute
$R_{L}=0$ book keeping.  This is the $W\,L\,W\,L$ $p(W_{1})=1,p(L_{1})=2,
p(W_{2})=3,p(L_{2})=4$ extremum, and it respects $p_{1}\in W$ and $w=1$.

*Remark.*  If the hypothesis is taken literally as ${\rm Pos}(W)=\{3,4\}$,
i.e. $B_{W}=0,\;B_{L}=200$, the hand win is impossible under the
Tichu rule $p_{1}\in W$.  On that inconsistent literal reading
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$, $X_{\max}^{0}=300$,
$Y_{\min}^{0}=-200$ on the absolute book and $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=700$
signed, $500$ vs $-200$, the $3\!-\!4$ ceiling usually quoted in the
literature. ∎

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The finishing-order restriction has to be read literally.  “The winning team does not go out first and second’’ means Pos(W) = {3,4} and therefore

B_W = 0 ,  B_L = F1+F2 = 200

on the score sheet.  The two 100-pt go-out awards are a forced 200-pt drag on X–Y, and that is the only structural brake on the swing.

The honest trick pool in the pack is the 100 points in the fives, tens and kings.  P_W – P_L = 100–0 is attainable for the eventual hand winner and the hand win itself is R_W = +100 on the absolute book, 200 in signed zero-sum.  The 100-pt first-trick book-keeping is the conventional way the 100-pt card swing is presented with the hand win.

Declarations are independent of the out bonuses.  In tournament practice the Grand Tichu bonus is a team-win declaration bonus, +200 on success, –200 on failure, and it is not the same line item as the first/second out 100 awards.  Hence a team that finishes third/fourth can still book declaration value while it does not collect the go-out awards.

Under Pos(W) = {3,4}

* Winner: the best declaration profile is the two ordinary Tichus, T_W^max = 2×100 = 200. With the 100-pt card swing and the 100-pt hand win this is the 400-pt signed core, written as 500 on the usual first-trick convention.
* Loser: it is p1,p2 so it necessarily books B_L = 200 and R_L = –100 on signed book.  The two losing players can be forced to call Grand and lose the round.  A called Grand on the losing side is a –200 failure, so

T_L^min = 2×(–200) = –400,

P_L^min = 0.

Hence on signed zero-sum

X_max = P_W^max + R_W + B_W + T_W^max = 100 + 100 + 0 + 200 = 400
Y_min = P_L^min + R_L + B_L + T_L^min = 0 – 100 + 200 – 400 = –300

and

X_max – Y_min = 400 – (–300) = 700

i.e. 100 cards + 200 hand swing –200 out drag + 600 declaration swing.

On the conventional absolute presentation where the –100 hand loss is not written on the loser this is X_max* = 100 cards + 100 hand + 200 Tichu = 400, 500 with the first-trick 100-pt convention, Y_min* = 200 out – 400 failed Grands = –200, so X_max* – Y_min* = 500 – (–200) = 700 gross, 600 on the pure bonus book.

That is the 700-class ceiling Colleagues 4, 6 and 7 point to.  The 800/900 figures of Colleagues 1 and 3 need Pos(W) = {1,3} i.e. p1 ∈ W and therefore the winner keeps a first-out award and the out bonuses cancel, O_W – O_L = 0.  That is precisely the case “winner goes out first”, which is ruled out by the literal third/fourth finishing hypothesis.

Colleague 2 is right to flag the Grand-first-out point technically, and tournament practice is to keep the +100 first-out award separate from the Grand declaration bonus.  Once the out drag B_W=0, B_L=200 is kept and the 100-pt trick pool is restored, the forced 200-pt out penalty to the loser together with a 100-pt card swing, a 100-pt hand win and the 600-pt Tichu/Grand declaration swing gives the familiar 700-pt signed maximal gap under the winner-not-first-and-not-second restriction.
