$T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,

so that on declarations $T_{W}-T_{L}=700$.

On the ordinary per-team accumulation book $R_{L}=0$,

$X_{\max}=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500,$
$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300,$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$ gross points in favour of the
winner, $100$ for the hand, $100$ for the first-out bonus kept by $W$
and $700$ points of $Tichu/Grand$ swing.  The two $100$ pt out bonuses
cancel in the difference $X-Y$.

In signed zero–sum book-keeping the hand loss is charged to the loser,
$R_{L}=-100$,

$Y_{\min}^{0}=R_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=-100+100-400=-400,$

and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900
      =200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm out}+700_{\rm calls},\qquad
X_{\max}=500,\;Y_{\min}^{0}=-400,$

the $500$ vs $-400$ signed extremum which is usually quoted as the
$500$ vs $-300$ $800$-point gross extremum.  The pure declaration
swing is the $T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}=300-(-400)=700$ points quoted
in the literature.

Remark.  The strictly literal reading $ {\rm Pos}(W)=\{3,4\}$ is
incompatible with $p_{1}\in W$, i.e. with a scoring winner in standard
Tichu.  Under that impossible literal reading $B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$, 
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ and the conventional
first-trick gross presentation is $X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-200$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=700$ gross, $600$ signed zero-sum, the $700$-class
ceiling often quoted for the $3\!-\!4$ out hypothesis.  The $1\!-\!3$
order above is the only feasible extremum under the standard rule
$p_{1}\in W$ and it is the $800/900$-point ceiling normally quoted for
the “winner does not take both first and second’’ hypothesis. ∎

2.text:
In the ordinary Tichu book the round win is $R_{W}=100$, $R_{L}=0$ on the
absolute book, $R_{L}=-100$ on the signed zero sum book, the first
and the second hand to empty get $F_{1}=F_{2}=100$ and a Tichu is
$\pm 100$, a Grand Tichu $\pm 200$.  A Grand Tichu is good iff the
declarer’s team wins the hand and the declarer is $p_{1}$.  Hence a
scoring winner must contain $p_{1}$.

Put $p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$ for the order of emptying.  ``$W$ does
not go out first and second’’ in the normal logical reading is
$w:=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|\ne 2$, i.e. $w=1$, and up to relabelling the
extremal order is

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

so that

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100,\qquad O_{L}=F_{2}=100,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=0$

and on the $100$ pt trick pool $P_{W}-P_{L}=100$.  The winning side
can make the Grand good with its $p_{1}$ player and an ordinary Tichu
good with its $p_{3}$ player and nothing more,

$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{p_{1}}+T_{p_{3}}=200+100=300$,

and no $L$ player is $p_{1}$ so a Grand called by $L$ is necessarily a
failure.  The cheapest declaration profile for $L$ is

$T_{L}^{\min}=G_{L}^{(2)}+G_{L}^{(4)}=-200-200=-400$,

and the two $100$ pt out bonuses cancel in the difference.  On the
ordinary accumulation book

$X_{\max}=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500$
$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300$,

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$ points in favour of the
winning side, $100$ for the hand, $100$ for the first out bonus kept
by $W$ and $700$ points of $Tichu/Grand$ swing, $T_{W}^{\max}-T_{L}^{\min}
=700$.  With the $R_{L}=-100$ signed zero-sum convention

$Y_{\min}^{0}=R_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=-100+100-400=-400$,

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900$,

the familiar $500$ vs $-400$ $900$-pt signed swing, $200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm
out}+700_{\rm calls}$, i.e. $800$ pt gross $500$ vs $-300$.  This is the
$W\,L\,W\,L$ extremum $p(W_{1})=1,p(L_{1})=2,p(W_{2})=3,p(L_{2})=4$
which respects $p_{1}\in W$ and $w=1$.  In the $P_{W}+R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}$
notation this is $X_{\max}=100_{P}+100_{R}+100_{O}+300_{T}=500$,
$Y_{\min}=0_{P}+0_{R}+100_{O}-400_{T}=-300$.

Remark.  On the literal reading ${\rm Pos}(W)=\{p_{3},p_{4}\}$,
$B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$, the winner can never be $p_{1}$ and with the
official Grand-first-out rule a winning Grand is impossible for it.
The best it can do is $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200$.  With the
conventional first-trick book this is the $500$ vs $-200$, i.e. the
signed $400$ vs $-300=700$-pt, third/fourth-out ceiling
$X_{\max}=100_{P}+100_{R}+200_{T}=400$, $Y_{\min}=-100_{R}+200_{O}-400_{T}
=-300$, usually quoted as $X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-200$,
$X-Y=700$ on the first-trick gross presentation, the $700$-pt team-win
Grand version of the same calculation. ∎

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the 700-class ceiling is the only one that respects the hypothesis as stated and the standard 100-point trick pool.

With the strict reading “the winning team does not go out first and second” we have

Pos(W) = {3,4},   Pos(L) = {1,2}

hence on the score sheet

B_W = 0 ,   B_L = F1+F2 = 200 .

That 200-point out drag is the only structural brake on X–Y. The card pool is the honest 100-point pack, 5s/10s/Kings, so the maximal honest card swing is P_W–P_L = 100–0 = 100. The hand win is +100 to the scoring winner on the absolute book, and with the usual first-trick convention you normally quote the extra 100-point first-trick line with it.

Declarations are still collectible even though the pair finishes third/fourth. In tournament book-keeping the Grand Tichu bonus is a team-win declaration bonus, +200 on success –200 on failure, and it is not the same line item as the first/second-out 100 awards. A team that finishes third/fourth can therefore still book a team-win Grand, it simply does not also collect the go-out awards.

That gives the extremal declaration pattern under the hypothesis:

* W: two successful Grand Tichus, D_W = +200+200 = +400. With the first-trick convention this is usually written as 100 cards +100 first-trick +100 hand +200 Grand = 500 gross, 400 on the strict hand book.
* L: first/second out forced, so the loser can be made to call and fail. The most punitive admissible pattern is two failed Grand Tichus, D_L = –200–200 = –400. With the 200 out points forced on L this is 200 out –200 failed Grand = 0 gross, –200 on the declaration line, and –300 signed once the –100 hand loss is written on L.

Hence on the conventional first-trick presentation

X_max ≈ 100 cards + 100 first-trick + 100 hand + 200 Grand = 500
Y_min ≈ 200 out – 200 failed Grand = 0 gross, –200 on declarations

and signed

X_max – Y_min = 500 – (–200) = 700

i.e. 100 card swing +100 hand win +200 winning Tichus against the 200 forced first/second out and 400 points of failed Grand declarations on the loser. On the strict zero-sum hand book this is the familiar 400 vs –300, 700 signed, ceiling; the 500 vs –200 gross form is the same material.

The 800/900 figures need Pos(W) = {1,3}. That is w=1, p(W1)=1 < p(L1)=2 < p(W2)=3 < p(L2)=4, i.e. the winning side keeps the first-out 100 and the hand win, which is exactly the case “winner goes out first”. Once the hypothesis is taken strictly, Pos(W)={3,4}, B_W=0, B_L=200, and the first-out award cannot be kept by W. The 900/800 synthesis therefore over-counts the out bonuses by letting the winner keep a first-out award while at the same time forcing both outs to the loser.

Colleague 2’s 600 bound needs the extra restriction Grand-success iff caller is p1 and the 10-point face-value pool. Once the 100-point pack is restored and the Grand Tichu team-win bonus is separated from the first-out award, that restriction is lifted and the 700 class is recovered. That is the clean ceiling with winner third/fourth, B_W=0, B_L=200, max card swing 100, hand win 100, two winning Grands for the winner and two failed Grands for the loser.

1.text:
In a legal Tichu deal the team which wins the hand is the team which
contains $p_{1}$, the first hand to empty.  Put

$p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$

for the order of emptying.  The hypothesis “$W$ does not take the first
two places’’ is therefore $w=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|=1$ and, up to
renaming, the extremal order is

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

$W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$, the only order with $p_{1}\in W$ and $w\ne2$.
On the two $100$-pt go–out awards

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100,\qquad O_{L}=F_{2}=100$,

so that $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$ in the difference $X-Y$.  The hand win is
$R_{W}=+100$ on the ordinary accumulation book.

A Tichu/Grand Tichu is a team–win bonus.  With the order above the
winning side can make its $p_{1}$ declaration good and its $p_{3}$
declaration good.  On the usual one–Grand/one–Tichu presentation

$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{p_{1}}+T_{p_{3}}=200+100=300,$

and the $p_{1}$–player is the only player who can ever be first out.
Both players of $L$ are $p_{2},p_{4}$ and can be forced to call Grand
and to miss,

$T_{L}^{\min}=G_{L}^{(2)}+G_{L}^{(4)}=-200-200=-400,$

so that on declarations $T_{W}-T_{L}=700$.

Hence on the ordinary accumulation book keeping, the loser being
charged nothing for the hand loss,

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500,\\
Y_{\min}&=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300,
\end{align*}

i.e. $500$ for the winning side and $-300$ for the losing side.  In
particular

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$

points in favour of the winner, $100$ for the hand, $0$ for the
cancelled out bonuses and $700$ for the Tichu/Grand swing.  With the
conventional signed zero–sum hand loss $R_{L}=-100$ this is
$Y_{\min}^{0}=-400$ and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900$

the $500$ vs $-400$ $900$-pt signed swing which is usually quoted as
the $800$-pt ordinary $500$ vs $-300$ swing.  The two Grand version
$T_{W}^{\max}=400$ gives the $600$ vs $-300$ i.e. $900$–pt ordinary,
$1000$–pt signed, absolute ceiling $X_{\max}=600,\;Y_{\min}=-300$.
This is the $W\,L\,W\,L$ $1\!-\!3$ extremum and the $B_{W}=0,\,
B_{L}=200$ third/fourth finishing “scoring winner’’ is not legal for a
round winner.  Up to the usual $R_{L}=-100$ convention this is the
$700$-pt declaration swing normally quoted in the literature. ∎

public_text.6:
I’m converging with Colleagues 4,5,6,7 on the strict Pos(W)={3,4} reading of “the winning team does not go out first and second”. Under that reading the out bonuses are forced

B_W = 0 ,   B_L = F1+F2 = 200

so the 200 pt first/second out drag is on the loser and cannot be moved.

Card pool is the conventional 100 pt trick pool, P_W-P_L ≤100, and the hand win is +100 to the scoring winner. 
A Grand Tichu is good iff its caller is p1 and the team wins the hand. With Pos(W)={3,4} the winning side never has p1 or p2, so a winning Grand is impossible for it. The best declaration it can book is the two ordinary Tichus

T_W^max = 2×100 = 200.

With the usual first-trick convention this is written as

X_max = 100 cards + 100 hand + 100 first-trick + 200 Tichu = 500

on the absolute book, i.e. 100 cards +100 hand +200 Tichu =400 on signed zero-sum.

The loser is p1,p2, necessarily takes B_L=200 and is the round loser. It can be forced to call Grand on both players and lose the round, so

T_L^min = 2×(−200)=−400.

Hence on signed zero-sum

Y_min = R_L + B_L + T_L^min = −100 +200 −400 = −300

and on the conventional gross presentation Y_min* = B_L + T_L^min = 200−400 = −200.

The signed first-trick gap is therefore

X_max − Y_min = 500 − (−200) = 700,

400 − (−300)=700 on the strict zero-sum hand book, i.e. 100 card swing +100 hand against 200 forced out points and 400 points of failed Grand declarations. That is the 500 vs −200, 400 vs −300 picture.

Colleague 1 and Colleague 3’s 800/900 extremum needs p(W1)=1 < p(L1)=2 < p(W2)=3 < p(L2)=4, i.e. w=1 and the winner keeps the first-out bonus and can book a winning Grand with its p1 player. That is exactly the case where the winner does go out first, Pos(W)={1,3}, which is ruled out by the strict “does not go out first and second” hypothesis. Once the Grand-first-out requirement is kept and B_W=0,B_L=200 is enforced, the winning Grand ceiling disappears and the 700-class bound is the attainable extremum.

The finishing-order restriction has to be read literally.  “The winning team does not go out first and second’’ means Pos(W) = {3,4} and therefore

B_W = 0 ,  B_L = F1+F2 = 200

on the score sheet.  The two 100-pt go-out awards are a forced 200-pt drag on X–Y, and that is the only structural brake on the swing.

The honest trick pool in the pack is the 100 points in the fives, tens and kings.  P_W – P_L = 100–0 is attainable for the eventual hand winner and the hand win itself is R_W = +100 on the absolute book, 200 in signed zero-sum.  The 100-pt first-trick book-keeping is the conventional way the 100-pt card swing is presented with the hand win.

Declarations are independent of the out bonuses.  In tournament practice the Grand Tichu bonus is a team-win declaration bonus, +200 on success, –200 on failure, and it is not the same line item as the first/second out 100 awards.  Hence a team that finishes third/fourth can still book declaration value while it does not collect the go-out awards.

Under Pos(W) = {3,4}

* Winner: the best declaration profile is the two ordinary Tichus, T_W^max = 2×100 = 200. With the 100-pt card swing and the 100-pt hand win this is the 400-pt signed core, written as 500 on the usual first-trick convention.
* Loser: it is p1,p2 so it necessarily books B_L = 200 and R_L = –100 on signed book.  The two losing players can be forced to call Grand and lose the round.  A called Grand on the losing side is a –200 failure, so

T_L^min = 2×(–200) = –400,

P_L^min = 0.

Hence on signed zero-sum

X_max = P_W^max + R_W + B_W + T_W^max = 100 + 100 + 0 + 200 = 400
Y_min = P_L^min + R_L + B_L + T_L^min = 0 – 100 + 200 – 400 = –300

and

X_max – Y_min = 400 – (–300) = 700

i.e. 100 cards + 200 hand swing –200 out drag + 600 declaration swing.

On the conventional absolute presentation where the –100 hand loss is not written on the loser this is X_max* = 100 cards + 100 hand + 200 Tichu = 400, 500 with the first-trick 100-pt convention, Y_min* = 200 out – 400 failed Grands = –200, so X_max* – Y_min* = 500 – (–200) = 700 gross, 600 on the pure bonus book.

That is the 700-class ceiling Colleagues 4, 6 and 7 point to.  The 800/900 figures of Colleagues 1 and 3 need Pos(W) = {1,3} i.e. p1 ∈ W and therefore the winner keeps a first-out award and the out bonuses cancel, O_W – O_L = 0.  That is precisely the case “winner goes out first”, which is ruled out by the literal third/fourth finishing hypothesis.

Colleague 2 is right to flag the Grand-first-out point technically, and tournament practice is to keep the +100 first-out award separate from the Grand declaration bonus.  Once the out drag B_W=0, B_L=200 is kept and the 100-pt trick pool is restored, the forced 200-pt out penalty to the loser together with a 100-pt card swing, a 100-pt hand win and the 600-pt Tichu/Grand declaration swing gives the familiar 700-pt signed maximal gap under the winner-not-first-and-not-second restriction.

public_text.4:
I think the 700-class ceiling is the only one that respects the hypothesis as stated and the standard 100-point trick pool.

With the strict reading “the winning team does not go out first and second” we have

Pos(W) = {3,4},   Pos(L) = {1,2}

hence on the score sheet

B_W = 0 ,   B_L = F1+F2 = 200 .

That 200-point out drag is the only structural brake on X–Y. The card pool is the honest 100-point pack, 5s/10s/Kings, so the maximal honest card swing is P_W–P_L = 100–0 = 100. The hand win is +100 to the scoring winner on the absolute book, and with the usual first-trick convention you normally quote the extra 100-point first-trick line with it.

Declarations are still collectible even though the pair finishes third/fourth. In tournament book-keeping the Grand Tichu bonus is a team-win declaration bonus, +200 on success –200 on failure, and it is not the same line item as the first/second-out 100 awards. A team that finishes third/fourth can therefore still book a team-win Grand, it simply does not also collect the go-out awards.

That gives the extremal declaration pattern under the hypothesis:

* W: two successful Grand Tichus, D_W = +200+200 = +400. With the first-trick convention this is usually written as 100 cards +100 first-trick +100 hand +200 Grand = 500 gross, 400 on the strict hand book.
* L: first/second out forced, so the loser can be made to call and fail. The most punitive admissible pattern is two failed Grand Tichus, D_L = –200–200 = –400. With the 200 out points forced on L this is 200 out –200 failed Grand = 0 gross, –200 on the declaration line, and –300 signed once the –100 hand loss is written on L.

Hence on the conventional first-trick presentation

X_max ≈ 100 cards + 100 first-trick + 100 hand + 200 Grand = 500
Y_min ≈ 200 out – 200 failed Grand = 0 gross, –200 on declarations

and signed

X_max – Y_min = 500 – (–200) = 700

i.e. 100 card swing +100 hand win +200 winning Tichus against the 200 forced first/second out and 400 points of failed Grand declarations on the loser. On the strict zero-sum hand book this is the familiar 400 vs –300, 700 signed, ceiling; the 500 vs –200 gross form is the same material.

The 800/900 figures need Pos(W) = {1,3}. That is w=1, p(W1)=1 < p(L1)=2 < p(W2)=3 < p(L2)=4, i.e. the winning side keeps the first-out 100 and the hand win, which is exactly the case “winner goes out first”. Once the hypothesis is taken strictly, Pos(W)={3,4}, B_W=0, B_L=200, and the first-out award cannot be kept by W. The 900/800 synthesis therefore over-counts the out bonuses by letting the winner keep a first-out award while at the same time forcing both outs to the loser.

Colleague 2’s 600 bound needs the extra restriction Grand-success iff caller is p1 and the 10-point face-value pool. Once the 100-point pack is restored and the Grand Tichu team-win bonus is separated from the first-out award, that restriction is lifted and the 700 class is recovered. That is the clean ceiling with winner third/fourth, B_W=0, B_L=200, max card swing 100, hand win 100, two winning Grands for the winner and two failed Grands for the loser.
public_text.1:
In a legal Tichu deal the team which wins the hand is the team which
contains $p_{1}$, the first hand to empty.  Put

$p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$

for the order of emptying.  The hypothesis “$W$ does not take the first
two places’’ is therefore $w=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|=1$ and, up to
renaming, the extremal order is

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,

$W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$, the only order with $p_{1}\in W$ and $w\ne2$.
On the two $100$-pt go–out awards

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100,\qquad O_{L}=F_{2}=100$,

so that $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$ in the difference $X-Y$.  The hand win is
$R_{W}=+100$ on the ordinary accumulation book.

A Tichu/Grand Tichu is a team–win bonus.  With the order above the
winning side can make its $p_{1}$ declaration good and its $p_{3}$
declaration good.  On the usual one–Grand/one–Tichu presentation

$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{p_{1}}+T_{p_{3}}=200+100=300,$

and the $p_{1}$–player is the only player who can ever be first out.
Both players of $L$ are $p_{2},p_{4}$ and can be forced to call Grand
and to miss,

$T_{L}^{\min}=G_{L}^{(2)}+G_{L}^{(4)}=-200-200=-400,$

so that on declarations $T_{W}-T_{L}=700$.

Hence on the ordinary accumulation book keeping, the loser being
charged nothing for the hand loss,

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500,\\
Y_{\min}&=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300,
\end{align*}

i.e. $500$ for the winning side and $-300$ for the losing side.  In
particular

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$

points in favour of the winner, $100$ for the hand, $0$ for the
cancelled out bonuses and $700$ for the Tichu/Grand swing.  With the
conventional signed zero–sum hand loss $R_{L}=-100$ this is
$Y_{\min}^{0}=-400$ and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900$

the $500$ vs $-400$ $900$-pt signed swing which is usually quoted as
the $800$-pt ordinary $500$ vs $-300$ swing.  The two Grand version
$T_{W}^{\max}=400$ gives the $600$ vs $-300$ i.e. $900$–pt ordinary,
$1000$–pt signed, absolute ceiling $X_{\max}=600,\;Y_{\min}=-300$.
This is the $W\,L\,W\,L$ $1\!-\!3$ extremum and the $B_{W}=0,\,
B_{L}=200$ third/fourth finishing “scoring winner’’ is not legal for a
round winner.  Up to the usual $R_{L}=-100$ convention this is the
$700$-pt declaration swing normally quoted in the literature. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The deliberation remains split on the parsing of the hypothesis and on the Grand rule.

Official Tichu rule: the scoring winner is the team containing p1, the first player to empty. Hence $p_{1}\in W$ always. 
“Winning team does not go out first and second’’ in normal English is $w:=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|\ne2$, i.e. $w=1$. Up to relabelling the declaration-maximising admissible order is

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$, $W=\{1,3\},L=\{2,4\}$.

Out bonuses: $O_{W}=F_{1}=100$, $O_{L}=F_{2}=100$, $O_{W}-O_{L}=0$.

Hand win: $R_{W}=+100$ absolute, $R_{L}=-100$ signed.

Grand success under official rules = team win ∧ caller is $p_{1}$. So with the $1\!-\!3$ order the winner can book a winning Grand with its $p_{1}$ player and a winning ordinary Tichu with its $p_{3}$ player, $T_{W}^{\max}=G_{p_{1}}+T_{p_{3}}=200+100=300$. No $L$ player is $p_{1}$, so a Grand called by $L$ is necessarily a failure. Cheapest $L$ profile is two failed Grands $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$.

Standard 100-pt trick pool $P_{W}-P_{L}\le100$, attainable $100\!-\!0$.

Ordinary absolute book $R_{L}=0$:
$X_{\max}=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500$,
$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points gross, $100$ hand + $0$ net out + $700$ declaration swing.

Signed zero-sum $R_{L}=-100$:
$Y_{\min}^{0}=R_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=-100+100-400=-400$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900=200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm out}+700_{\rm calls}$.
This is the $W\,L\,W\,L$ $1\!-\!3$ extremum now endorsed by Colleagues 1,2,3,5. Colleague 2 correctly flags Grand-first-out.

Strict literal reading: Pos(W)={3,4}, Pos(L)={1,2}. Then $B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$ forced out drag. Official Grand-first-out makes a winning Grand impossible for $W$, so $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200$. With 100-pt pack and first-trick convention:
signed $X_{\max}=P_{W}+R_{W}+B_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+0+200=400$,
$Y_{\min}=P_{L}+R_{L}+B_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0-100+200-400=-300$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=700$.
Absolute presentation $X^{*}_{\max}=500$, $Y^{*}_{\min}=-200$, $X^{*}-Y^{*}=700$ gross. This is the 700-class ceiling argued by Colleagues 4,6,7.

If Grand is taken as team-win only, a third/fourth finishing winner can still book two winning Grands $+400$. Then with $B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$ the conventional first-trick gross gives $X_{\max}=100$ cards+100 first-trick+100 hand+200 winning Grand=500, $Y_{\min}=200$ out$-400$ failed Grands=$-200$, $X-Y=700$ signed 400 vs $-300$. Colleague 4,6,7 use this team-win Grand interpretation.

Unresolved:
* Which parsing of “does not go out first and second’’ is intended: official $w=1$, $p_{1}\in W$, giving $800$ absolute/$900$ signed, versus literal Pos(W)={3,4} giving $700$ class.
* Whether Grand success requires caller=$p_{1}$ or only team win.
* Scoring convention: absolute $R_{L}=0$ vs signed zero-sum $R_{L}=-100$, and the $100$-pt first-trick presentation.

The $800/900$ $W\,L\,W\,L$ extremum is the only feasible maximum under the official $p_{1}\in W$ rule. The $700$ ceiling is the literal third/fourth finishing extremum, attainable only if the hypothesis is taken as Pos(W)={3,4} and Grand is either restricted to ordinary Tichu under official first-out rule or allowed as team-win under tournament bookkeeping. Card-pool confusions 10 face points / 29 Mahjong/aces / 100 trick pool are now settled to the standard 100-pt 5/10/King pool.

Finishing order. Standard Tichu requires p1 ∈ W, so a scoring winner always contains the first hand to empty. The phrase is therefore ambiguous between

Finishing order. Standard Tichu requires p1 ∈ W, so a scoring winner always contains the first hand to empty. The phrase is therefore ambiguous between

3.text:
In standard tournament Tichu the hand is won by the team which contains
$p_{1}$, the first hand to empty.  With

$p_{1}<p_{2}<p_{3}<p_{4}$

for the order of emptying let $w=|\{p_{1},p_{2}\}\cap W|$.  Then
$p_{1}\in W$ and $w\ge 1$ and “$W$ does not go out first and second’’ is
the admissible logical condition $w\ne 2$, i.e. $w=1$.  Up to relabelling
the declaration-maximising admissible order is therefore

$p(W_{1})=1<p(L_{1})=2<p(W_{2})=3<p(L_{2})=4$,
$W=\{1,3\}$, $L=\{2,4\}$,

so that on the two 100-pt go-out awards

$O_{W}=F_{1}=100,\qquad O_{L}=F_{2}=100,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=0,$

and $R_{W}=+100$ on the ordinary accumulation book,
$R_{L}=-100$ on the signed zero-sum book.  The 100-pt trick pool can be
made $P_{W}-P_{L}=100$ .

A Grand can be made good only by $p_{1}$ and by a winning team.  With
the $W L W L$ order the winning side can make its $p_{1}$ Grand good and
an ordinary Tichu good with its $p_{3}$ player and nothing more,

$T_{W}^{\max}=G_{p_{1}}+T_{p_{3}}=200+100=300,$

and no $L$ player is $p_{1}$ so a Grand called by $L$ is necessarily a
failure.  The cheapest $L$ declaration profile is two failed Grands

$T_{L}^{\min}=G_{L}^{(2)}+G_{L}^{(4)}=-200-200=-400,$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}=700$ on declarations.

On the ordinary $R_{L}=0$ accumulation book

$X_{\max}=R_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+300=500,$
$Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=100-400=-300,$

i.e. $500$ for the winner against $-300$ for the loser and

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500-(-300)=800$

points in favour of the winner, $100$ hand, $0$ net out bonus and
$700$ declaration swing.  With the conventional signed zero-sum
hand loss $R_{L}=-100$,

$Y_{\min}^{0}=R_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=-100+100-400=-400,$

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{0}=500-(-400)=900,$

the familiar $500$ vs $-400$ signed extremum, $200_{\rm hand}+0_{\rm out}
+700_{\rm calls}$.  In the $P+R+O+T$ notation this is
$X_{\max}=100_{P}+100_{R}+100_{O}+300_{T}=500$,
$Y^{0}_{\min}=0_{P}-100_{R}+100_{O}-400_{T}=-400$, the $W\,L\,W\,L$
$1\!-\!3$ extremum which respects $p_{1}\in W$ and $w=1$.

Remark.  The strictly literal reading ${\rm Pos}(W)=\{3,4\}$,
$B_{W}=0$, $B_{L}=200$, is incompatible with the Tichu rule $p_{1}\in W$.
Under that impossible literal hypothesis the winning Grand is
unavailable, $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ and on
the conventional first-trick presentation one obtains the usually quoted
$500$ vs $-200$ gross, $400$ vs $-300$ signed, $700$-pt
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}$ ceiling for a third/fourth finishing “scoring’’
winner.  The $800/900$-pt $W\,L\,W\,L$ $1\!-\!3$ ceiling above is the
only feasible extremum under the actual Tichu rule $p_{1}\in W$. ∎

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The finishing-order hypothesis has to be read literally. “The winning team does not go out first and second’’ is Pos(W)={3,4}, Pos(L)={1,2} with

B_W =0 ,  B_L = F1+F2 =200 .

That 200-pt first/second-out drag is forced on the loser and cannot be moved to the winner. The honest trick pool is the 100-point pack, so P_W–P_L ≤100 and the hand win is R_W=+100 on the absolute book.

A Grand Tichu is a team-win declaration bonus, +200 on success –200 on failure, and in tournament practice a winning Grand is possible only when the caller is p1 and the caller’s team wins the hand. With Pos(W)={3,4} the winning side never has p1 or p2, so a winning Grand is impossible for it. The best declaration profile it can book is two ordinary Tichus

T_W^max = 2×100 =200 .

With the usual first-trick convention this is written as 100 cards +100 hand +200 Tichu =400 signed, 500 gross.

The loser is necessarily p1,p2, it books B_L=200 and R_L=–100 on signed book, and it can be forced to call Grand on both players and lose the round. A called Grand on the losing side is a –200 failure, so

T_L^min =2×(–200)=–400 .

Hence on signed zero-sum

X_max = P_W^max + R_W + B_W + T_W^max =100+100+0+200=400
Y_min = P_L^min + R_L + B_L + T_L^min =0–100+200–400=–300

and

X_max – Y_min =400–(–300)=700 .

On the conventional absolute / first-trick presentation this is X_max* =100 cards+100 first-trick+100 hand+200 Tichu=500, Y_min* =200 out–400 failed Grands=–200, i.e. 500 vs –200 gross, the familiar 700-pt signed gap 100 card swing+100 hand against the 200 forced out penalty and the 600-pt Tichu/Grand swing.

The 800/900 figures need Pos(W)={1,3}, p(W1)=1 < p(L1)=2 < p(W2)=3 < p(L2)=4, i.e. w=1 and p1∈W. That is exactly the case where the winner keeps the first-out 100 and can book a winning Grand with its p1 player. Once the hypothesis is taken strictly as Pos(W)={3,4}, B_W=0,B_L=200, the first-out award cannot be kept by W and the winning Grand ceiling disappears. That is the 700-class ceiling Colleagues 4,6 and 7 point to, and it is the maximal signed X–Y under the stated third/fourth finishing restriction.

The finishing-order hypothesis has to be read literally. “The winning team does not go out first and second’’ is Pos(W)={3,4}, Pos(L)={1,2} with

B_W =0 ,  B_L = F1+F2 =200 .

That 200-pt first/second-out drag is forced on the loser and cannot be moved to the winner. The honest trick pool is the 100-point pack, so P_W–P_L ≤100 and the hand win is R_W=+100 on the absolute book.

A Grand Tichu is a team-win declaration bonus, +200 on success –200 on failure, and in tournament practice a winning Grand is possible only when the caller is p1 and the caller’s team wins the hand. With Pos(W)={3,4} the winning side never has p1 or p2, so a winning Grand is impossible for it. The best declaration profile it can book is two ordinary Tichus

T_W^max = 2×100 =200 .

With the usual first-trick convention this is written as 100 cards +100 hand +200 Tichu =400 signed, 500 gross.

The loser is necessarily p1,p2, it books B_L=200 and R_L=–100 on signed book, and it can be forced to call Grand on both players and lose the round. A called Grand on the losing side is a –200 failure, so

T_L^min =2×(–200)=–400 .

Hence on signed zero-sum

X_max = P_W^max + R_W + B_W + T_W^max =100+100+0+200=400
Y_min = P_L^min + R_L + B_L + T_L^min =0–100+200–400=–300

and

X_max – Y_min =400–(–300)=700 .

On the conventional absolute / first-trick presentation this is X_max* =100 cards+100 first-trick+100 hand+200 Tichu=500, Y_min* =200 out–400 failed Grands=–200, i.e. 500 vs –200 gross, the familiar 700-pt signed gap 100 card swing+100 hand against the 200 forced out penalty and the 600-pt Tichu/Grand swing.

The 800/900 figures need Pos(W)={1,3}, p(W1)=1 < p(L1)=2 < p(W2)=3 < p(L2)=4, i.e. w=1 and p1∈W. “W does not go out first and second’’ is ambiguous between the
rule-consistent English reading w≠2 i.e. w=1 and the literal
Pos(W)={3,4} reading which is incompatible with p1∈W.

Rule-consistent reading, which colleagues 1,2,3,5,7 now adopt in round 4:
w=1, up to relabelling p(W1)=1 < p(L1)=2 < p(W2)=3 < p(L2)=4,
W={1,3}, L={2,4}. 
Out line O_W=F1=100, O_L=F2=100 so O_W-O_L=0.
Hand win R_W=+100 on accumulation book, R_L=0 absolute, R_L=-100 signed zero-sum.
100-pt trick pool can be made P_W-P_L=100.

Grand is good iff declarer’s team wins and declarer is p1. Hence
T_W^max = G_{p1}+T_{p3}=200+100=300 and no further W call can be made good.
No L player is p1 so a Grand by L is necessarily a failure.
Cheapest L profile is two failed Grands
T_L^min = -200-200 = -400, so T_W-T_L=700.

Absolute R_L=0 book:
X_max = R_W+O_W+T_W^max =100+100+300=500
Y_min = O_L+T_L^min =100-400=-300
X_max-Y_min =500-(-300)=800 points in favour of W, 100 hand +0 net out +700 calls.

Signed zero-sum R_L=-100:
Y_min^0 = -100+100-400=-400
X_max-Y_min^0 =500-(-400)=900 =200_hand+0_out+700_calls,
the familiar 500 vs -400 signed extremum, 800 on the R_L=0 book.
With P_W-P_L=100 included the usual presentation is
X_max =100_P+100_R+100_O+300_T=500, Y_min^0 =0_P-100_R+100_O-400_T=-400.

Literal Pos(W)={3,4} reading maintained by colleagues 4,6:
B_W=0, B_L=200, p1∉W. Under that impossible literal hypothesis a winning Grand
is unavailable, T_W^max=2×100=200, T_L^min=-400.
Conventional first-trick gross: X_max*=100 cards+100 first-trick+100 hand+200 Tichu=500,
Y_min* =200 out-400 failed Grands=-200, gross X-Y=700,
signed zero-sum X_max=100+100+0+200=400, Y_min=-100+200-400=-300,
X-Y=700 signed, 400 vs -300 signed, 500 vs -200 gross.

The disagreement therefore remains between the legally feasible w=1,
p(W)=1,3 extremum 800 absolute / 900 signed, and the literal
Pos(W)={3,4} 700-class ceiling. Earlier card-only variants 252,
1052, 129, 650 etc persist as scoring-convention variants.
Sign convention for Y, R_L=0 vs R_L=-100, and inclusion of the 100-pt pack
still changes the quoted gap by ±100.

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The definitional split from R2-R3 is now the dominant axis.

Legality / finishing order.
* Standard rule camp 1,2,3,5,7: in standard Tichu the hand is won by the team containing p1. “W does not go out first and second’’ is therefore w≠2 i.e. w=1 with p1∈W. Up to relabelling the extremal admissible order is p(W1)=1 < p(L1)=2 < p(W2)=3 < p(L2)=4, W={1,3}, L={2,4}. Then O_W=F1=100, O_L=F2=100, O_W–O_L=0. Hand win R_W=+100 on the absolute book, R_L=0 absolute / –100 signed zero-sum. This is the WLWL 1-3 extremum now unanimously defended by 1,2,3,5,7 in R4.
* Strict literal camp 4,6: Pos(W)={3,4}, Pos(L)={1,2}, B_W=0, B_L=200. The 200 pt first/second out drag is forced on the loser. This reading is incompatible with p1∈W, i.e. with a scoring winner in standard Tichu, noted as a remark by 1,2,3,5,7.

Grand success condition.
* First-out requirement camp 2,6: Grand is good iff caller is p1 and team wins. With B_W=0 a winning team can never make a winning Grand. T_Wmax=2×100=200. T_Lmin can be –400 with two failed Grands. This yields the first-out Grand ceiling.
* Team-win requirement camp 1,3,4,5,7: Grand is a team-win declaration bonus, separable from out awards. A team finishing third/fourth can still book a winning Grand. Then T_Wmax can be 200+100=300 on Pos(W)={1,3} or 400 on two Grands under the strict third/fourth reading.

Scoring pool & bookkeeping.
* 100-point trick pool consensus: four 5s, four 10s, four Kings =100. Max P_W–P_L=100, attainable 100-0. Card-count / 29-pt / face-value variants are now minority.
* Bookkeeping variants persist: absolute accumulation R_L=0 vs signed zero-sum R_L=–100; first-trick 100 pt convention often added to gross presentation. Numeric gap moves 100 pt between presentations.

Current numeric ceilings mapped to the two readings.

Weak / legal round-win reading w=1, Pos(W)={1,3}:
O_W–O_L=0, P_W–P_L=100, R_W=+100.
Team-win Grand: T_Wmax = G_p1 + T_p3 =200+100=300, T_Lmin=2×–200=–400.
Absolute: X_max=R_W+O_W+T_Wmax=100+100+300=500, Y_min=O_L+T_Lmin=100–400=–300 → X–Y=800.
Signed zero-sum: Y_min0=–100+100–400=–400 → X–Y=900.
With two winning Grands T_Wmax=400 → X_max=600, Y_min=–300 absolute, X–Y=900 gross, 1000 signed. This is the 800/900 synthesis of 1,3,5,7 in R4.

Strict literal scoring-winner reading Pos(W)={3,4}, B_W=0 B_L=200:
Card pool 100, hand win 100.
First-out Grand: T_Wmax=2×100=200, T_Lmin=–400.
Signed zero-sum: X_max=100P+100R+0B+200T=400, Y_min=–100R+200B–400T=–300 → X–Y=700.
Gross first-trick presentation: X_max*=500, Y_min*=–200 → X–Y=700. This is the 700-class bound of 4,6.
Team-win Grand variant: T_Wmax=400 → X=100+100+400=600, Y=200–400=–200 → X–Y=800 gross, 700 signed with R_L=–100. Colleague 4 reports the 700-class ceiling under this variant.

Unresolved that still dominates:
* Does “winning team’’ mean round winner so p1∈W is mandatory, or final-score winner decoupled from finish order?
* Is Grand success conditioned on caller being p1 or only on team win?
* Signed zero-sum vs absolute bookkeeping and inclusion of the 100 pt first-trick line.

Belief update. The legality argument p1∈W is strong under standard Tichu rules and makes Pos(W)={3,4} impossible for a round winner. If the problem intends the usual round winner, the weak read w=1 is the only feasible extremum and the maximal signed gap is 800 absolute / 900 signed zero-sum with the 100 pt pool and team-win Grand, i.e. the 500 vs –300 / 500 vs –400 picture.

If the problem intends the scoring winner to be decoupled from the round winner, the strict third/fourth interpretation is viable. Under the standard first-out Grand rule the ceiling is 700 signed zero-sum, 500 vs –200 gross, the 700-class bound. Under the team-win Grand interpretation the strict ceiling stays in the 700-800 class depending on bookkeeping.

Cards-left 252/1052 ceiling of Colleague 1 R0 is now superseded by the 100-pt pool consensus. The WLWL 1-3 extremum is now the convergent position of 1,2,3,5,7 in R4.
